documents.t: Restman is a command-line tool written in Python, designed to combine the simplicity of cURL with the powerful features of Postman. It aims to relieve users from the complexities of manually building network connections with URLs or endpoints, allowing them to focus solely on the core aspects of HTTP requests and responses. With Restman, users can quickly and efficiently test APIs, handle different HTTP methods, and parse response data without worrying about the underlying connection mechanics.

In Python development practice, debugging is an indispensable part of the process. If you rely on print() statements to trace the execution flow of your program, you might encounter persistent exceptions that are difficult to pinpoint even after multiple code reviews. This is often due to the limitations of this debugging method as the terminal output grows, making it hard to correlate outputs with their corresponding function calls. This article introduces the IceCream library, a specialized debugging tool that significantly enhances debugging efficiency, making the entire process more systematic and standardized.

Dazhi Zhang (Tony) Senior Software Developer · Engineering Leader · AI Architect Time can fade everything (416) ***-****✉️ googol.zhang@gmail.com A well-qualified software developer, a fast learner, a highly motivated self-starter, and a reliable person to work with. I design the architecture of enterprise data and AI platforms at Scotiabank, and outside the enterprise I build the WhereQ Universe — one centralized data cloud serving a family of applications across FinTech, geo technology, booking, logistics, learning, private media and retro computing. Professional Experience WhereQ Inc. Owner · 2020 – Present Founder of WhereQ Inc., where I design the architecture of the WhereQ Universe — one centralized data cloud that serves every application in it, and a family of products across FinTech, geo technology, booking, logistics, learning, private media and retro computing. Designed the architecture of the universe: one centralized data cloud (whereq.cloud) — a versioned, metered API and MCP server over 25M+ named records — serving every application below. Built the FinTech products on top of that cloud: flowdesk.top (NOVA, the AI market-research analyst) and caijing.today (Chinese-first financial news, hot rankings and an economic calendar). Built whereq.com, the geo technology layer: maps, routing, places and neighbourhood boundaries — plus the crawler and the schema it reads. Built chroniq.cc, a scheduling engine that respects holidays, lunar dates, weather and 8 languages. Built qhaul.ca, an Uber-style moving, delivery and haulage platform running on local drivers across the GTA. Built catobigato.com, an AI tutoring assistant for K-12 to college that explains, quizzes and graphs its work. Built whereq.cc, a self-encrypted photo vault with AI tagging and enhancement — the key never leaves the device. Built whereq-dosbox, a complete DOS emulator built natively for Android: the emulator core runs as libdosbox.so inside an APK, and it plays most vintage DOS games and software. Shipped keytomarvel.com as the identity layer every application signs in through, whereq.ca as the research station where ideas are tested before they graduate, and this site as the universe’s public voice. Constructed a scheduled batch service to retrieve selling data and display it on an integrated Google Map website. Designed and implemented a proprietary image compression algorithm to reduce Amazon S3 costs. Developed a ChatGPT-like console with categorized prompts and integrated Google Social Login. Built comprehensive API sets using Spring WebFlux for efficient communication with OpenAI endpoints. Established tech stack using jHipster, React, Spring WebFlux, PostgreSQL, and Keycloak. Orchestrated infrastructure setup on AWS EC2 and RDS for production services. Stack: Amazon EC2, RDS, S3, Spring WebFlux, React, Keycloak, Angular, GIS, Google Map, MapStruct, Git, CI/CD, Social Login Scotiabank Lead Engineer · 04/2019 – Present Tech leader and solution architect for the BNS data platform — big data streaming, metric collection, performance tuning and automation — and for the enterprise AI initiatives built on top of it. Led the architecture and delivery of enterprise AI initiatives, including Data GPT and internal GenAI enablement platforms, achieving the 90-90 KPI — 90% query accuracy, with 90% of queries answered within 30 seconds. Built Data GPT, an AI-powered query platform using OpenAI’s GPT-3.5 Turbo model to deliver accurate and efficient data retrieval for enterprise-grade analytics. Evaluated and integrated emerging AI technologies, establishing reusable frameworks and best practices for enterprise adoption. Designed and implemented "Spark as a Service" and an Avro/JSON flattener service. Developed lightweight scaffolding using Spring Boot, R2DBC, and MapStruct to simplify API development. Led end-to-end solution design for data consumption using Presto, connecting HDFS, ElasticSearch, and PostgreSQL. Developed ElasticSearch metrics tools and centralized business calendar services using Node.js and PostgreSQL. Reengineered Credit 360 application, improving performance, codebase, and validation frameworks. Stack: Kubernetes, Docker, Presto, Spark, Kafka, HDFS, ElasticSearch, Power BI, Java, Spring Boot, Angular, MongoDB, Jenkins, PostgreSQL, OpenAI GPT-3.5, GenAI, Git TD Bank Senior Software Developer · 11/2018 – 04/2019 Developed new features and contributed to the EasyApply program, focusing on Java backend systems and automated testing frameworks. Introduced POJO generation from JSON schemas for validation purposes. Developed a retry module using Java 8 Functional Interfaces and the template method design pattern. Built 10 new API endpoints within three months and refactored existing components. Stack: Java, Spring, Oracle 12c, Jenkins, Postman, MQ, Git, Hibernate Rogers Communications Inc. Senior Software Developer · 08/2016 – 09/2018 Full-stack developer and architect leading the evolution of the Enterprise Notification System (ENS), improving performance and introducing new features. Integrated an SMS Gateway using SMPP protocol to enhance SMS delivery performance. Re-architected the ENS for better scalability, handling over a million email notifications per hour. Introduced RESTful interfaces and optimized system performance. On this page The collections Threads All pages The WhereQ Atlas A wiki of the universe and its craft The WhereQ Universe is a family of applications built on one centralized data cloud. The Atlas is where they are written down — alongside the standards and tools they are built on, and the vocabulary they share. Pages 30 Collections 4 Threads 4 Terms 30 The collections Four collections, each with its own kind of page. The Universe is what WhereQ builds; the References shelf is what it is built from; the DOS Games are what runs on WhereQ-DOSBox; the Glossary is the language the rest of it uses. Pages 5 Groups 3 In the Atlas 4collections What this shelf is A shelf of DOS games, each one documented the way a person who has just installed it would want it read: here is the bundle, here is exactly what you have to do to start it, and here is what every key does. These are the games that run on WhereQ-DOSBox — the DOS emulator built natively for Android, one page away in the Universe. They were tested on an emulator running the app, and the steps on each page are the steps that actually worked, including the ones that turned out to be wrong on the first attempt. This shelf holds the games that have been played through on an emulator. Every other game in the archive has a page too, in the catalogue at /dos-games/ — the facts read out of the bundle itself, with a download and the setup its shape implies. Those pages say plainly that nobody has played them yet. The shape of every page stays the same as the shelf grows. How to read a game page Each page runs in the same order: what the game is, the download with its checksum, the setup in WhereQ-DOSBox, how to play it, what is inside the bundle, and where every fact came from. The download comes first on purpose — the page is worth little if the reader has to hunt for the file. Every page also carries a notice about the download, and every page carries a comment thread. If a step does not work on your device, or you know a shorter way in, say so in the comments — that is what the thread is for. The whole archive The shelf above holds the games that have been played through on an emulator. The catalogue behind it holds every game in the archive — one page each, with the facts read out of the bundle itself, the download, and the setup the bundle's own shape implies. Those pages say plainly that nobody has played them yet, and each one carries a comment thread for whoever gets there first. Open the catalogue — every DOS game in the archive About the downloads The archives on these pages are published for study, communication and preservation only. They are the work of their authors and publishers, who hold the rights in them; publishing one here claims none of those rights and waives none of them. If you believe a download here breaks a licence, a copyright or any other right, tell us and we will take it down. The same goes for a bundle that is missing something — say so in the comments and it will be replaced. The directory Everything in this collection, grouped. Open one to read its full page in the Atlas. M — names that start with “M”1 page The games on this shelf whose name begins with M. 真人快打The Fighting Game The 1993 DOS conversion of Midway's arcade fighter, published by Acclaim and converted by Probe. It imports, Play starts it, and then it sits there looking dead — because the copy-protection screen wants a word and the title screen wants F1. Both are written down. 1993Download the bundle S — names that start with “S”3 pages The games on this shelf whose name begins with S. 三国志英杰传The Strategy RPG The 1995 KOEI strategy RPG in its Traditional Chinese DOS release. You play Liu Bei, gathering officers and holding the line against Dong Zhuo and the Cao Wei campaign that follows. It is the one game on this shelf that refuses to start when you press Play — it needs a different launcher, and the page says which one. 1995Download the bundle 沙丘魔堡The Real-Time Strategy The 1992 Cryo and Virgin Games real-time strategy game, in the Chinese release published by 第三波. Import the zip, press Play, and the batch file runs the intro and the game for you. The one thing the page has to explain is the house-selection screen: it is mouse-driven, and a quick tap moves the cursor without clicking. 1992Download the bundle 三国志IIIThe Grand Strategy The third of KOEI's Three Kingdoms games, in its Simplified Chinese DOS release. Import the zip, then change one line: the app starts MAIN.EXE on its own and the game exits at once — the launcher is KOEI.COM. Once that is set, the whole game opens: the opening cards with their poems, the dragon and the tiger, six scenarios from 189 to 235, and a map of China you run a war from. 1993Download the bundle Y — names that start with “Y”1 page The games on this shelf whose name begins with Y. 炎龙骑士团II‧黄金城之谜The Fantasy Strategy The 1995 sequel to 炎龙骑士团, in its Traditional Chinese DOS release. Import the zip and press Play: the app picks FD2.EXE and the game runs, intro animation and all. The page writes down the route in — which key skips the film, how the story dialogue advances, how you move on the field map, and how a battle is fought down to the damage and the experience points. 1995Download the bundle Comments Missing a game, or a step that does not work on your device? On this page What it is Download the bundle Set it up in WhereQ-DOSBox How to play What is in the bundle Where the facts come from DOS GamesThe Fighting Game 真人快打 Mortal Kombat for DOS — launches straight, then hides the key that starts it. Download the bundle About this download The archive on this page is published for study, communication and preservation only. 真人快打 (Mortal Kombat) is the work of Midway Games and Acclaim Entertainment and of the people who made the DOS conversion, and those rights are theirs; publishing it here claims none of them and waives none of them. If you believe this download breaks a licence, a copyright or any other right, tell us and we will take it down. 真人快打 at a glance Role The Fighting Game Collection The DOS Games Domain M — names that start with “M” Developer Probe Software — the DOS conversion team Published Acclaim Entertainment, 1993 Platform MS-DOS (DOS/4GW, 386) Genre Fighting game Fighters Kano, Johnny Cage, Rayden, Liu Kang, Scorpion, Sub-Zero, Sonya, Goro, Shang Tsung Entry point MK.EXE — picked automatically Bundle 67 files · 3,128,439 bytes Status 1993 What it does Nine fighters — Kano, Johnny Cage, Rayden, Liu Kang, Scorpion, Sub-Zero, Sonya, Goro and Shang Tsung — each with its own strengths and finishing move. Story mode with a biography screen for every fighter, from the Black Dragon clan's own recruitment pitch to Shang Tsung's island fortress. MIRROR MATCH, and three levels of ENDURANCE for the tournament. Sound through the AdLib, Roland and Sound Blaster drivers, all of which are in the bundle and all of which can be chosen in the game's own setup. The game's own setup screen, on F10, where every control can be re-assigned to the key of your choosing. See also whereq-dosboxUniverse Go to Download the bundle What it is 真人快打 is the DOS version of Mortal Kombat — the Midway arcade fighter that arrived on the PC in 1993 as a DOS/4GW program. The credit inside MK.EXE reads "THE PROBE CONVERSION TEAM:", so Probe Software did the conversion, and Acclaim published it. The strings and the graphics files inside the archive name both: ACCLAIM.GRA and PROBE.GRA. The dates in the archive agree with that. The data files run from May 1993 to December 1993, and the game itself carries the line "ALLOW 4-6 WEEKS FOR DELIVERY — OFFER EXPIRES NOVEMBER 1, 1993". The roster is the arcade one, with two extra: Kano, Johnny Cage, Rayden, Liu Kang, Scorpion, Sub-Zero and Sonya, plus Goro and Shang Tsung. The fight modes are MIRROR MATCH and three levels of ENDURANCE. Download the bundle The archive is the upstream file, byte for byte. The checksum below is what you should get. Field Value File mortal-kombat.zip Size 3,128,439 bytes SHA-256 79d860d2acf89533be69bfe93f298b58309dedae14c721f2b24b12d4ab50aa75 Contents 67 files — the game, its graphics and its sound drivers Source dos-bin.zczc.cz — the archive this page was generated from Download 真人快打.zip (3.0 MB) Set it up in WhereQ-DOSBox This one is the easy case: import the zip, and the app finds MK.EXE on its own and Play starts the game. There is no launcher to set, no driver to load first. Import the zip into WhereQ-DOSBox — open it from the Files app on your phone and choose WhereQ-DOSBox, or use the app's own import. Tap Play. The game starts. One thing to leave alone: the bundle contains CRACK.COM, and you should not run it. It prints "File Was NOT Successfully Patched!" and changes nothing — the MK.EXE in this archive is already the finished WOLVERINE crack, so there is nothing left to patch. Running it only wastes a DOS prompt. The bundle also ships the four sound drivers of the period — ADLIB.DRV, ROLAND.DRV, SBLASTER.DRV and BEEP.DRV. Which one the game picks is up to the sound card DOSBox presents, so if the music is thin, that is the setting to change rather than anything in the archive. How to play Here is the part that is not written down anywhere. The game starts, and it looks stuck. First screen: a copy-protection prompt that asks for a word. Type any word and press Enter — it takes anything. Then the title screen and the attract cycle. Press F1 to start the game. F1 only works while the start screen is up. If a demonstration match is playing, keep pressing F1 — pressing it during a match starts story mode instead. On the on-screen keyboard, F1 lives in the Fn layer. On a Bluetooth or USB keyboard, press F1 directly: WhereQ-DOSBox forwards hardware keys into DOSBox. From F1 you get CHOOSE YOUR FIGHTER. The arrows move the cursor and a punch key — S by default — confirms the fighter you are pointing at. In the match itself the arrows move, the same keys punch and kick, and F10 opens the game's own setup. That setup screen is worth knowing. CONTROL 1: KEYBOARD is where every action is bound: the game asks you to press the key for UP, for DOWN, for LEFT, for RIGHT, then HIGH PUNCH, LOW PUNCH, BLOCK, HIGH KICK and LOW KICK, and whatever you press is what it uses. Because WhereQ-DOSBox forwards a hardware keyboard into DOSBox, you can bind any key you like. The same screen sets the difficulty (VERY EASY to VERY HARD), the speed (LOW (386) or HIGH (486)), the sound card (NO SOUND, SPEAKER, ADLIB, ROLAND, SOUND BLASTER, or ROLAND & SBLASTER) and the control device. Verified on the emulator: Sonya against Raiden and Sub-Zero against Kano both start, the fighter moves when the arrow is pressed, and the opponent's health bar goes down. What is in the bundle File What it is MK.EXE The game. This is what Play starts. DOS4GW.EXE The 32-bit DOS extender the game runs under. CRACK.COM A patcher for the shareware release. Nothing to patch here — leave it alone. ACCLAIM.GRA, PROBE.GRA The publisher's and the developer's title graphics. KANO.GRA, NINJA.GRA, RAIDEN.GRA, EMP.GRA, … The graphics of the fighters, one file each. KATT.GRA, SCATT.GRA, SZATT.GRA, … The fighters' stance and attacking poses. S1HDRS.GRA, FU1HDRS.GRA, MPHDRS.GRA, … The header files the game reads each fighter with. SAMPLES.DAT The sound samples. ADLIB.DRV, ROLAND.DRV, SBLASTER.DRV, BEEP.DRV The sound drivers. Where the facts come from The game itself — the copy-protection screen, the title cycle, the fighter select and a live match, all read on the emulator. MK.EXE's own strings: "THE PROBE CONVERSION TEAM:", "OFFER EXPIRES NOVEMBER 1, 1993", and the filenames it opens. The dates on the files inside the archive, May to December 1993. On this page What it is Download the bundle Set it up in WhereQ-DOSBox How to play The password screen What is in the bundle Where the facts come from DOS GamesThe Grand Strategy 三国志III KOEI's 1993 war of the Three Kingdoms — and it will not start unless you change the command the app runs. Download the bundle About this download The archive on this page is published for study, communication and preservation only. 三国志III is the work of KOEI CO., LTD. and of the people who made it; publishing it here claims none of their rights and waives none of them. If you believe this download breaks a licence, a copyright or any other right, tell us and we will take it down. 三国志III at a glance Role The Grand Strategy Collection The DOS Games Domain S — names that start with “S” Developer KOEI CO., LTD. (光荣) — named in the bundle's own FM sound driver Published 1993 — 23 of the bundle's 35 files carry that year Platform MS-DOS — 16-bit real mode Genre Grand strategy — territories, cities, officers and battles Language Simplified Chinese Entry point KOEI.COM — you have to set this by hand Bundle 35 files · 2,260,444 bytes Status 1993 What it does Six scenarios, from 靈帝沒落 董卓進京 in 189 to 臥龍歸天 姜維繼志 in 235 — each one starts on a different date, in a different situation. A map of the whole of China, with cities in the colour of their lord, roads, rivers and mountains, and the armies drawn as flags on it. A full command set at the top of the screen — 休養, 軍事, 人事, 外交, 情報, 開發, 謀略, 商人, 特別 and 功能 — and a market panel quoting the price of rice, bows and horses. A roster of every officer with his 武力, and a conscription that takes men away from the city and puts them under a general. An opening of cards: a dithered picture — a warrior's head, a city gate — with a poem written down it in vertical columns. See also whereq-dosboxUniverse Go to Download the bundle What it is 三国志III — Romance of the Three Kingdoms III, in its Simplified Chinese DOS release. It is a grand strategy game: a map of the whole of China, the cities on it, the officers who hold them, and the markets they trade in. The archive calls it 三国志III, and this copy is the Chinese one — every word on the screen is 简体. The bundle names its own maker. FMDRV.COM — the FM sound driver the launcher loads — carries the line "Copyright (C) 1991 KOEI CO.,LTD. JAPAN", and the game's own DOS shell is KOEI.COM. That shell is written into the bundle's SHELL.SYS, the file DOS reads at boot to decide what the command prompt is. The copy is dated 1993: 23 of its 35 files carry that year, and the game's own program, MAIN.EXE, is dated 3 January 1994. The Chinese text is all there — the menus, the scenario list, the officers' names and the orders you give them are in 简体, not in a Japanese or English release. The whole game is one directory of plain files: three executables, two COM loaders, the Chinese 16-dot fonts, six scenario files and a stack of .DAT data files. Nothing is compressed and nothing needs installing. Download the bundle This is the original copy from the archive the page was generated from. The checksum below is what you should get. Field Value File 三国志3.zip Size 2,260,444 bytes SHA-256 515ec3ed07caf4948a92923388350ade12df279807c2510b0fdb51bf39f95216 Contents 35 files — the game, its data and its DOS shell Source dos-bin.zczc.cz — the archive this page was generated from Download 三国志3.zip (2.2 MB) Set it up in WhereQ-DOSBox There is one thing to change, and the app will not do it for you. Import the zip, open the game's row and tap Launch… — the command the app would run by itself is MAIN.EXE, and MAIN.EXE on its own exits immediately and drops you back at the DOS prompt. The launcher is KOEI.COM. Import the zip into WhereQ-DOSBox — open it from the Files app on your phone and choose WhereQ-DOSBox, or use the app's own import. Open the game's row and tap Launch…. Tap Clear, then tap the KOEI.COM chip. The script line reads KOEI, and that is right — DOS adds the .COM itself. Tap Play. The app writes a RUN.BAT in the game folder and runs KOEI from it. What KOEI.COM does, in order: it loads FMDRV.COM as the resident sound driver, then runs OPEN.EXE, then MAIN.EXE, and END.EXE when the game ends. The names are all in the launcher's own strings, in that order. There is no installer to run and nothing to configure. Do not run OPEN.EXE or END.EXE yourself — KOEI.COM runs them for you, in the right order. How to play The opening is a run of cards. Each one is a dithered picture — a warrior's head in blue, a city gate — with a poem written down it in vertical columns. The first is 滾滾長江東逝水，浪花淘盡英雄, the poem that opens the Romance; the later ones tell the Yellow Turban rising — 十常侍弄權柄，陷害忠良亂朝廷。中平元年關癘氣，大賢良師他自稱。張角舉事造黃旗. Space moves the cards along. The cards are followed by the password screen, and then the dragon and the tiger, and a card that says 「使用滑鼠時，請按滑鼠鍵. 使用鍵盤時，請接著鍵入.」 — use the mouse, or press a key to type. Press Enter and the title menu comes up: 1. 開始新遊戲, 2. 從進度檔案載入進度, 3. 登錄新武將. Every menu in this game is a numbered one. Type the number and press Enter. A new game asks, in order: how many people are playing (0 to 8), which of the six scenarios, which lord you are, how hard (初級 or 高級), whether you want to watch the other countries' wars first, and whether it is 史實型 (history happens) or 假想型 (history does not). It then shows the whole setup back to you and asks 全部都可以了嗎(Y/N)?. The main screen is a map of China. Across the top is the command row — 0.休養 1.軍事 2.人事 3.外交 4.情報 5.開發 6.謀略 7.商人 8.特別 9.功能 — and the bottom line asks you what you want to do: 『劉備，請向23.新野下命令(0-9)?』. The panel on the right is the city you are standing in: its population, its gold, its grain, its soldiers, its officers and its mood, with the market prices beside it and your ruler's portrait below. Under 軍事 there are nine more: 移動, 輸送, 戰爭準備, 戰爭, 徵兵, 募兵, 訓練, 再編成 and 造船. Taking 徵兵 asks 派誰徵兵(0-13)? and opens a roster of your officers with their 武力; type the number of the officer you want, press Enter, and the game asks 徵兵幾百人(1-38)?. The men are taken, the city's soldiers go up, and the leftover is offered to another general. One wrinkle worth knowing: when a roster of names is on screen, typing the number does not select the officer straight away — it moves the marker to that entry and marks it with a star. Press Enter as well, and the game takes it. Verified on the emulator: the game starts from the KOEI.COM launcher, the opening cards and the dragon and tiger play, the title menu opens, a new game is set up from scratch, the map of China comes up, the 軍事 menu opens, and 徵兵 was carried through to the end — 100 soldiers recruited and the city's numbers changed. A battle was not fought, and the password screen was passed with the word "abc" rather than the one the game shows. The password screen After the opening cards, before the dragon and the tiger, the game asks 密碼: and, under it, 請輸入正確密碼 with the answer in red brackets — [孫李李]. That is the copy-protection screen, and in this release it does not check: the word "abc" was typed, Enter pressed, and the game carried on as if it had been right. So you do not have to type 孫李李 — and you cannot easily, since the on-screen keyboard has no Chinese characters on it. Type anything and press Enter. What is in the bundle File What it is KOEI.COM The launcher — 694 bytes, and the file named in SHELL.SYS. It chains FMDRV.COM → OPEN.EXE → MAIN.EXE → END.EXE. FMDRV.COM The resident FM sound driver. Carries "Copyright (C) 1991 KOEI CO.,LTD. JAPAN". OPEN.EXE, MAIN.EXE, END.EXE The three programs the launcher runs, in that order. MAIN.EXE is dated 3 January 1994, and on its own it exits at once — the chain is not optional. SHELL.SYS Ten bytes: KOEI.COM. It is what DOS boots into. SANGOKU3.SAV The save file. HAN.16P, NAME.16P The fonts the game draws its Chinese text with — .16P is a 16-pixel dot font. SNDATA1–6.CIM, SNDATA1–6B.CIM The six scenarios, and a second set beside each of them. MAPDATA.DAT, GRPDATA.DAT, KAODATA.DAT, PACKDATA.DAT, … The map, the graphics, the officer data and the rest of the game's data. Where the facts come from The game itself — the opening cards, the password screen, the dragon and the tiger, the title menu, the scenario list, the map of China, the 軍事 menu and the 徵兵 that was carried through, all read on the emulator. FMDRV.COM's own string: "Copyright (C) 1991 KOEI CO.,LTD. JAPAN". KOEI.COM's own strings: the four programs it chains, and its error messages — "DISK ERROR HIT ENTER to RETRY", "Not enough memory.", "$ : cannot execute.", "$ : file access failure.", "$ : password error occurred." SHELL.SYS out of the archive: KOEI.COM. On this page What it is Download the bundle Set it up in WhereQ-DOSBox How to play What is in the bundle Where the facts come from DOS GamesThe Strategy RPG 三国志英杰传 KOEI's 1995 war-and-campaign classic — and the one that will not start unless you tell it how. Download the bundle About this download The archive on this page is published for study, communication and preservation only. 三国志英杰传 is the work of KOEI CO., LTD (© 1995 KOEI CO.,LTD) and of the people who made it; publishing it here claims none of their rights and waives none of them. If you believe this download breaks a licence, a copyright or any other right, tell us and we will take it down. 三国志英杰传 at a glance Role The Strategy RPG Collection The DOS Games Domain S — names that start with “S” Developer KOEI CO., LTD Publisher KOEI CO., LTD — Taiwan release by 第三波 (Soft-World) Published 1995 Platform MS-DOS Genre Strategy RPG (S-RPG) Language Traditional Chinese (Big5) Entry point REKO3.COM — not MAIN.EXE Bundle 60 files · 3,461,749 bytes Status 1995 What it does A campaign map: you move Liu Bei and the officers who have joined you between cities, and each move leads to a battle. Officers who join you, level up, and carry the treasure and horses you give them — the treasure in particular changes how a battle ends. A story that follows the Romance of the Three Kingdoms from the coalition against Dong Zhuo through to the campaign against Wei. A story prologue that plays before the first battle, and an ending sequence of its own after the last. See also whereq-dosboxUniverse Go to Download the bundle What it is 三国志英杰传 — Romance of the Three Kingdoms: Heroic Legend — is KOEI's 1995 strategy role-playing game. You take the role of Liu Bei, and the campaign runs from the coalition that marches on Dong Zhuo through the long fight against Cao Wei. Officers join you as the story goes on, they level up, and what you equip them with decides how a battle ends. This bundle is the Traditional Chinese DOS release, not the Japanese original: the text inside it is Big5, and the publisher of the Chinese release was 第三波 (Soft-World). The screen is VGA text mode with an animated status bar, and the game speaks in the voice of the 1990s Chinese translation — 開始新遊戲 for a new game, 讀取存檔 to load one, 功能設定 for the options, 觀看劇情簡介 to watch the story prologue. The copyright line on the title screen reads © 1995 KOEI CO.,LTD, and the graphics credit inside the executable reads "TF-SSC … Programmed by T.FUJINUMA (TF-928) 1994,1995". The archive's installer string dates the release to 17 February 1995. Download the bundle The archive is the upstream file, byte for byte. The checksum below is what you should get. Field Value File sanguo-yingjie-zhuan.zip Size 3,461,749 bytes SHA-256 07bad92d786dbcd90bf27eed6e8473e09374608e21767c68d11cf293b3982999 Contents 60 files — the game, its drivers and its data Source dos-bin.zczc.cz — the archive this page was generated from Download 三国志英杰传.zip (3.4 MB) Set it up in WhereQ-DOSBox This is the part that catches people out. Pressing Play on this bundle does not start the game — it drops you at a DOS prompt and nothing else happens. The game is not broken; it is waiting for the right launcher. Import the zip into WhereQ-DOSBox — open it from the Files app on your phone and choose WhereQ-DOSBox, or use the app's own import. Open the game's row and tap Launch… to open the launch script. Tap Clear to empty the script field. Tap the REKO3.COM chip to put REKO3 in the script field. Tap Play. REKO3.COM is the game's own launcher, and it is the only thing that starts the game correctly. It loads the sound driver (SBOPL2.COM), the graphics driver (GRPDRV.EXE) and the font driver (TFDED.COM), and then runs OPEN.EXE for the intro, MAIN.EXE for the game itself and END.EXE for the ending. It also needs the game on two drives. WhereQ-DOSBox already mounts A: and B: to the game folder, which is what REKO3 expects — the game reads A:BAKDATA.R3 and B:IPPAN0.R3 — so there is nothing to mount by hand. Why Play on its own fails: the app picks the biggest executable that is not an installer or a driver, and in this bundle that is MAIN.EXE. MAIN.EXE is the game without its drivers and without the launcher, so it starts, cannot draw, and falls back to the DOS prompt. Run INSTALL.EXE and you make it worse — the archive is already the installed layout. How to play The first thing you see is a password prompt: 密碼, with the line 請輸入正確密碼 [木土日] underneath. Type anything at all and press Enter — the gate takes whatever you type and lets you through into the menu. It is a copy-protection gate, not a secret; the 木土日 hint belongs to something else inside the game. The menu has four items: 開始新遊戲 (new game), 讀取存檔 (load a save), 功能設定 (options) and 觀看劇情簡介 (watch the story prologue). They are mouse-driven — the keyboard will not move that cursor. Give DOSBox the mouse: press RMB on the on-screen keyboard (or the right mouse button on a Bluetooth keyboard) to switch mouse capture on, then tap the screen to click. Tap 開始新遊戲 to start a new campaign. Press Enter on the KOEI logo screen to move into the story prologue, then keep pressing Enter to step through it. From there the campaign proper begins: the map, the officers, the battles. Two things worth knowing before you start. The campaign is decided in the planning stages — which officers you bring, which treasure and which horse each of them carries, and how you spend your turns — so the map matters more than the fighting does. And if you want to see how far Liu Bei can go, the strategy guides for this game describe a way to raise him straight to level 99: in a non-battle state, move the arrow onto Liu Bei's portrait and hold the left mouse button, then answer 是 when the question comes up, and do the same with the bead at the top left. What is in the bundle File What it is REKO3.COM The launcher. Run this one — it chains the drivers, the intro, the game and the ending together. MAIN.EXE The game itself, and the file the app picks on its own. Runs without its drivers. OPEN.EXE / END.EXE The story prologue and the ending sequence. GRPDRV.EXE The graphics driver. SBOPL2.COM The sound driver. TFDED.COM The font driver — this is what puts the Chinese text on the screen. BAKDATA.R3, IPPAN0.R3 Save and campaign data. BAKDATA.R3 is read from A:, IPPAN0.R3 from B:. INSTALL.EXE The 1995 installer. You do not need it — the archive is already installed. Where the facts come from The game itself — the title screen, the menu, the prompt and the in-game credits, read on the emulator. The executable's own strings: "© 1995 KOEI CO.,LTD", "TF-SSC … Programmed by T.FUJINUMA(TF-928) 1994,1995", and the installer string "KOEI Install Program Ver 2.4 / 1995/ 2/17". The archive listing and checksum of the upstream file. Wikipedia, for the release date and the Taiwanese publisher. The Chinese strategy guides (par.com.tw and the 巴哈姆特 board), for the campaign structure and the level-99 trick. ← Back to The DOS Games · Next: 真人快打 Comments Got a step that does not work on your device, or a shorter way in? On this page What it is Download the bundle Set it up in WhereQ-DOSBox How to play What is in the bundle Where the facts come from DOS GamesThe Real-Time Strategy 沙丘魔堡 Dune II in its Chinese release — it starts on its own, and then asks you to click a house. Download the bundle About this download The archive on this page is published for study, communication and preservation only. 沙丘魔堡 is the work of Cryo Interactive and Virgin Games and of the people who made the Chinese release; publishing it here claims none of their rights and waives none of them. If you believe this download breaks a licence, a copyright or any other right, tell us and we will take it down. 沙丘魔堡 at a glance Role The Real-Time Strategy Collection The DOS Games Domain S — names that start with “S” Developer Cryo Interactive — with Virgin Games Publisher Virgin Games; the Chinese release by 第三波 (Soft-World) Published 1992 Platform MS-DOS Genre Real-time strategy Language Traditional Chinese (Big5) Entry point DUNE.BAT — picked automatically Bundle 136 files · 1,743,136 bytes Status 1992 What it does A real-time strategy game on Arrakis: you build on the map, the enemy house builds back, and the spice is what you are both fighting over. Two houses — Atreides and Harkonnen — with their own units, buildings and commanders. A mission map you can open at any time, with the troop positions of every house on it. Hot-seat for two players on one screen: the panel at the bottom of the screen carries the number of each house. See also whereq-dosboxUniverse Go to Download the bundle What it is 沙丘魔堡 is the Chinese release of Dune II — the 1992 real-time strategy game from Cryo Interactive and Virgin Games. The Chinese title is 第三波's own: the intro screen reads VIRGIN GAMES under a Chinese line that says 第三波文化事業 1992 強強滾推出, and the whole game is in Traditional Chinese. The archive carries the original installer, and it names the authors: INSTALL.EXE holds the line "(c) 1992 Cryo & Virgin Games". That is the game as it shipped — on floppies, with the first disk called out in the installer's own text, "INSERT DUNE DISK 1 IN DRIVE A:". The Chinese release is a translation of the whole thing, not just the interface: the introduction is narrated in Chinese ("在未來的世界裡 人類已發現了無數的星系…"), the map is called 沙丘地圖, and the build panel speaks in the language of the 1990s Chinese localisation. Download the bundle The archive is the upstream file, byte for byte. The checksum below is what you should get. Field Value File sha-qiu-mo-bao.zip Size 1,743,136 bytes SHA-256 982268c362a646be6454e8fce29c036a8ce1a1a38710f09c260806c621d5d641 Contents 136 files — the game, its data and its original installer Source dos-bin.zczc.cz — the archive this page was generated from Download 沙丘魔堡.zip (1.7 MB) Set it up in WhereQ-DOSBox This one needs no setup at all. The bundle has exactly one batch file, DUNE.BAT, and the app picks it on its own — so import the zip and press Play. Import the zip into WhereQ-DOSBox — open it from the Files app on your phone and choose WhereQ-DOSBox, or use the app's own import. Open the game's row and tap Play. The app starts DUNE.BAT. DUNE.BAT turns the sound off, plays the intro logo and starts the game with the switches the release was made for. The whole of DUNE.BAT is three lines: @echo off, logo, and then duneprg CHIVGA SDB22227 EMS 386. The first runs LOGO.EXE, which is the Virgin and 第三波 title card. The second starts DUNEPRG.EXE with the language and display switches for the Chinese text on VGA, a Sound Blaster setting, and expanded memory on a 386. Do not run INSTALL.EXE. It is the 1992 floppy installer: it wants DUNE DISK 1 in drive A:, asks for 2 500 KB of free space, and copies the game to C:\DUNE. The archive is already the installed layout — the installer would only put the game in the wrong place. How to play The intro plays first: the Virgin Games logo, then the Chinese line naming 第三波, and then a narrated introduction over a desert scene. Press Space on the on-screen keyboard to step through the narration — one press, one line. Then the house-selection screen comes up: a throne room, the name of a house on the panel at the bottom, and the mouse cursor. This is the one screen where the mouse matters, and the app needs a little care with it. Give DOSBox the mouse first: press RMB on the on-screen keyboard (or the right mouse button on a Bluetooth keyboard) to switch mouse capture on. Move the cursor with the arrow keys on the on-screen keyboard. The cursor is the arrow on the picture; the arrow keys move it. A quick tap only moves the cursor — it does not click. Hold the press for about half a second before letting go, and the click lands. Click the house crest at the top-left or the top-right of the screen to take that house. Click the player number in the panel at the bottom — 1 or 2 — to confirm, and the world map comes up. The world map is 沙丘地圖, and the panel below it reads 結束地圖模式 — that is the hint for the control pad on the right, and pressing it takes you back out of the map. The panel carries the numbers of the houses in play, so a second player can take the other house on the same screen. Verified on the emulator: the intro plays, the house is taken, and the world map opens with the base on it and the map panel showing the troop count. The build phase was not played through — that is the next thing to work out, and the comments on this page are where it should go. What is in the bundle File What it is DUNE.BAT The launcher the app starts. Plays the logo, then the game. DUNEPRG.EXE The game itself. LOGO.EXE The Virgin Games and 第三波 title card, played by the batch file. INSTALL.EXE The 1992 floppy installer. Do not run it — the archive is already installed. *.HSQ The game's data: the map, the units, the buildings, the dialogue, the manual. *.AGD, *.M32 The same data in other formats — the game's own compression and its 32-bit build. FONT16.16P The bitmap font the game draws its text with. TABLAT.BIN, VERBIN.BIN The building table and the version block. DUNE23S0.SAV, DUNE23S3.SAV, DUNE23S4.SAV Saved games that came with the release. WOR16.FON, WOR16.ASC The word font — this is what puts the Chinese text on the screen. Where the facts come from The game itself — the intro card, the narrated introduction, the house-selection screen and the world map, all read on the emulator. DUNE.BAT, read out of the archive: @echo off, logo, duneprg CHIVGA SDB22227 EMS 386. INSTALL.EXE's own strings: "(c) 1992 Cryo & Virgin Games", "INSERT DUNE DISK 1 IN DRIVE A:", "Free disk space= 2500 Kb", and the files it writes. On this page What it is Download the bundle Set it up in WhereQ-DOSBox How to play The field map, the command ring and a landed attack What is in the bundle Where the facts come from DOS GamesThe Fantasy Strategy 炎龙骑士团II‧黄金城之谜 Dynasty's fantasy strategy game — it starts on its own, and the first chapter plays as a film. Download the bundle About this download The archive on this page is published for study, communication and preservation only. 炎龙骑士团II‧黄金城之谜 is the work of 漢堂國際資訊股份有限公司 (Dynasty International Information Co., Ltd) and of the people who made it; publishing it here claims none of their rights and waives none of them. If you believe this download breaks a licence, a copyright or any other right, tell us and we will take it down. 炎龙骑士团II‧黄金城之谜 at a glance Role The Fantasy Strategy Collection The DOS Games Domain Y — names that start with “Y” Developer 漢堂國際資訊 — Dynasty International Information Co., Ltd Published 1995 — the newest date inside the bundle is 18 January 1995 Platform MS-DOS — 32-bit protected mode (DOS/4GW) Genre Strategy RPG (戰棋) with tactical battles Language Traditional Chinese (Big5) Entry point FD2.EXE — picked automatically Sound Miles Design Audio Interface Library V3.02, of 18 January 1995 Bundle 47 files · 8,155,666 bytes Status 1995 What it does An opening chapter that plays as a film: a castle under the moon, the two kings on their thrones, and Saul before his father. A field map you walk around a tile at a time, with characters who talk when you walk into them. A tactical layer under the story: a command ring of four icons around the selected character — physical attack, spell attack, items, rest — that ends in a real battle. Move a character next to an enemy, take the attack from the ring, and the screen darkens into a night scene with a sword coming down: the pirate loses HP and the game hands out 31 experience points. A full sound system in the bundle — the Miles Design library, with drivers for the Ad Lib, the Roland, the Sound Blaster, the Tandy and the Yamaha, and SETSOUND.EXE to pick one. The game data in plain files: the animations in ANI.DAT, the character shapes in FDSHAP.DAT, the fields in FDFIELD.DAT, the text in FDTXT.DAT and the icons in FDICON.B24. See also whereq-dosboxUniverse Go to Download the bundle What it is 炎龙骑士团II‧黄金城之谜 — Fantasy War 2, in its Traditional Chinese DOS release. The title screen names the company that made it: 漢堂, under the English line DYNASTY INTERNATIONAL INFORMATION CO., LTD. It is a 32-bit program. FD2.EXE is a DOS/4GW executable — Rational Systems' protected-mode run-time, copyright 1987 to 1993 — carrying a WATCOM C/C++ 32-bit run-time of its own. The bundle's own newest date is the audio library, Miles Design Audio Interface Library V3.02 of 18 January 1995, which is where the 1995 comes from. The sound is set up already. DIG.INI and MDI.INI both point at a Creative Labs Sound Blaster 16 on port 220h — SB16.DIG and SBPRO2.MDI — so the game has sound without any setup of your own. Download the bundle This is the original copy from the archive the page was generated from. The checksum below is what you should get. Field Value File 炎龙骑士团II‧黄金城之谜.zip Size 8,155,666 bytes SHA-256 bd241b639ad5e122faf6996e4dd000fdd3b2a5d7bd55709df17db517e9962ed1 Contents 47 files — the game, its data and its sound drivers Source dos-bin.zczc.cz — the archive this page was generated from Download 炎龙骑士团II‧黄金城之谜.zip (7.8 MB) Set it up in WhereQ-DOSBox There is nothing to set up. The bundle has one executable that matters, FD2.EXE, and the app finds it on its own — so import the zip and press Play. Import the zip into WhereQ-DOSBox — open it from the Files app on your phone and choose WhereQ-DOSBox, or use the app's own import. Open the game's row and tap Play. The app writes a RUN.BAT in the game folder and runs FD2 from it. Wait. The first thing on the screen is the DOSBox banner, and then the game's own title animation. Do not run SETSOUND.EXE unless the sound is wrong. It is the Miles configuration tool, and it writes DIG.INI and MDI.INI — which are already in the archive, already pointing at a Sound Blaster 16 on port 220h. The game reads them as they are. How to play The opening is a film, and it is a long one: a castle under the moon, a face made of red brush strokes, the 漢堂 card, and the silver 2 over the red wordmark. Press Space on the on-screen keyboard to skip through it. After the film comes the title menu: START, LOAD and CONTINUE, in English, on a blue screen with a red banner. Space starts a new game — the mouse does not work on this screen, so use the keyboard. Then the story plays as a dialogue, with a portrait on the right and the text on the left. The first line is 『兒臣索爾，晉見父王陛下』 — Saul before his father the king — and in the throne room a little later: 『到這裡來，讓义王好好看看你。這一陣子國務繁忙，我們父子兩個也很久沒聚聚了』. Space, Enter and Escape all move the dialogue along. After the story you are on the field: a map of grass and paths, with your character standing on it and other people around. The arrow keys move. Walk into someone and the game starts talking to them — the first character you meet says 『……唉！』 and the game goes on from there. Verified on the emulator: the game starts from Play with nothing else to do, the title menu comes up, the intro and the story play, the Chinese text is all there, the character walks on the map and the conversations start. The field map and the battle interface were then taken apart as well — the next section writes down what is on the screen, what each key does, and how a battle is fought from the first move to the experience points. The field map, the command ring and a landed attack The field map is a tile grid that the camera follows. The arrow keys move the cursor one tile at a time, and the little panel in the bottom-right corner always describes the tile the cursor is standing on: a picture of the ground plus the attack and defence modifiers that the terrain gives. Plain ground reads A+05 D+00, and a forest reads A-05 D+10 — the forest's pair is exactly what the game's own rules give for 森林 (−5% AP, +10% DP). Stand the cursor on one of your own people and press Space or Enter, and the game opens that character's window: name, class, level, HP, MP, DX, MV, HIT, AP, EV, DP, and the equipment with the AP and DP it adds. 悠妮 is a 人類 法師 at LV.01 with EX·00, HP 028/028, MP 008/008, DX·001, MV·04, HIT·086, AP·011, EV·001 and DP·007; 亞雷斯 is a 人類 騎士 at LV.01 with EX·00, HP 048/048, MP 000/000, DX·002, MV·07, HIT·092, AP·026, EV·002 and DP·006, carrying a 刺矛 (+AP 020) and 布衣 (+DP 002); 蓋亞 is a 機械 機兵 at LV.01 with HP 050/050, MP 000/000, DX·002, MV·04, HIT·092, AP·022, EV·002 and DP·014, carrying a 威力手臂 (+AP 015) and a 戰鬥裝甲 (+DP 008). Around the selected character the game draws a ring of four command icons, and the layout is the one the game's own player notes describe: 上 physical attack, 左 spell attack, 右 items, 下 rest. The attack icons are drawn on a red plate and the other two on a blue one — the red plate is the command that is usable at that moment, and Space, Enter and Ins confirm it. The spell icon animates with sparks around it. Press Space on the character and the ring opens; press it again on a mage and the spell list comes up — 悠妮 knows one spell, 火炎術, priced at MP 02. Stand on empty ground, press Space, and a different ring opens instead: the field menu with 系統選單, 行軍, 設定 and 結束本回合, and Enter on it opens the system menu, which reads MAP·01 TURN·001, lists the victory condition 敵全滅 and the failure condition 索爾死亡, and counts the field as ENEMY·07 FRIEND·04 NPC·00 with ¥00000000 in the treasury. F1 opens the global map — the whole field at a glance, with our side in blue and the enemy in red. The enemy on this map is a group of masked pirates, red headband over a dark visor, and their numbers are readable: put the cursor on one and the panel shows its HP (028) as it shows a character's. Moving a character is two steps. Put the cursor on one of your own people and press Space: the game enters 進行移動, the character's stats appear in the panel at the top left, and the arrow keys now walk the cursor around while the tile panel follows it. Press Space again and the character walks to the tile the cursor was standing on. We moved 亞雷斯 three tiles west and two tiles south, from the path in the north to the grass next to a pirate. Standing next to the enemy brings the command ring up around 亞雷斯, and now 物理攻擊 is the one on the red plate — the others turn blue. Space picks the target: the cursor jumps onto the pirate and its HP shows in the panel. One more Space lands the hit. The screen darkens into a night scene with a crescent moon and a sword comes slashing down, with 亞雷斯 LV·01 HP 048 MP 000 on one side and 盜賊 LV·02 on the other. The pirate went from 028 HP to 007 HP, and the game paid for the hit: 得到經驗31點！ — 31 experience points, shown on a panel with the character's portrait. Press Space on the enemy itself and the game opens its whole sheet: 盜賊, 人類 盜賊, LV·02, HP 007/028, EX 007/028, DX·002, MV·04, HIT·097, AP·024, EV·002, DP·004, carrying a 短劍 (+AP 010) and a 布衣 (+DP 002). What is still open: the enemy turn. The 結束本回合 entry of the field menu is reachable — Ins on it pops 要結束本回合的行動嗎？ with YES and NO and 悠妮's portrait — but the answer could not be given from the app, so the enemies have not been seen to move or to strike back. The ring also only ever confirms its red entry: the direction keys moved the map cursor but never changed which icon the ring had picked, and neither did long key holds, Android key events, the numeric keypad scancodes, or taps and drags on the icons themselves. That is what the comments on this page are for. The control scheme above is the game's own, not ours: the four commands around a character and the four entries of the field menu are laid out exactly as the game's player notes and the Chinese walkthroughs describe them — 人物處按確定：上面：物理攻擊，左面：法術攻擊，下面：休息，右面：物品裝備, and 空白處按確定：上=系統選單，左=行軍，右=設定，下=結束本回合. 炎龍騎士團2 新手提示 — the game's own player notes (chiuinan.github.io) 《炎龙骑士团2黄金城之谜》最全游戏攻略 — the command layout (bilibili) What is in the bundle File What it is FD2.EXE The game. This is what Play starts. ANI.DAT The animations — the intro, the portraits, the map figures. FDSHAP.DAT, FDFIELD.DAT, FDOTHER.DAT The character shapes, the fields and everything else the game draws with. FDTXT.DAT, TITLE.DAT The text, and the title-screen data. FDICON.B24 The icons. FDMUS.DAT, TAI.DAT The music. FD2.SAV, FD2.TMP The save file and its working copy. DIG.INI, MDI.INI The Miles sound configuration, already set for a Sound Blaster 16 on 220h. SETSOUND.EXE The Miles configuration tool. You do not need it. SB16.DIG, SBPRO2.MDI, ADLIB.MDI, ROLAND.MDI, TANDY.MDI, YAMAHA.MDI, … The sound drivers — one for each kind of card the library knows. SAMPLE.AD, SAMPLE.OPL, SAMPLE.BNK The instruments and the sound banks. Where the facts come from The game itself — the DOSBox banner, the title animation, the 漢堂 card, the opening dialogue, the field map, the command ring, the character windows, the global map, the system menu and a whole battle: the move, the target, the night attack scene, the damage and the experience award, all read on the emulator. The game's own player notes for the control scheme — 新手提示 (操作): 方向鍵 = 移動游標, Space/Enter/Ins+己方人員：進行移動，移動後 上=攻擊，左=施法，右=物品，下=休息, Space/Enter/Ins+空地：上=系統選單，左=行軍，右=設定，下=結束本回合, and the terrain table that gives 一般 +5% AP / −5% DP and 森林 −5% AP / +10% DP. The Chinese walkthrough for the ring layout — 人物處按確定：上面：物理攻擊，左面：法術攻擊，下面：休息，右面：物品裝備 — and 空白處按確定：上=系統選單，左=行軍，右=設定，下=結束本回合. The title screen's own line: DYNASTY INTERNATIONAL INFORMATION CO., LTD. FD2.EXE's own strings: "DOS/4G Copyright (C) Rational Systems, Inc. 1987 - 1993" and the WATCOM C/C++ 32-bit run-time. DIG.INI and MDI.INI out of the archive: "Miles Design Audio Interface Library V3.02 of 18-Jan-95", SB16.DIG and SBPRO2.MDI at 220h. documents.t: On this page How to read this The terms The WhereQ Atlas The Glossary The vocabulary the Universe and the References shelf share, defined once. Every term links to the pages where it actually turns up. Terms 30 How to read this A term is worth defining only if the definition removes a misunderstanding. These are the ones that do — the words that mean something slightly different to different people, or that carry a consequence worth knowing before you rely on them. Where a term appears on a page in the Atlas, that page is linked under the definition. Follow one to see the term in use. The terms ACID The four guarantees a transactional database offers: Atomicity (a transaction is all or nothing), Consistency (constraints hold after it commits), Isolation (concurrent transactions do not see each other's partial work) and Durability (a committed transaction survives a crash). PostgreSQL Apache Kafka Backpressure The mechanism by which a system that cannot keep up with its input slows the producer down, instead of letting an unbounded queue build. Without it, the slowest component decides how much memory the whole system needs. Apache Kafka Apache Spark CDC — Change Data Capture Reading the stream of changes out of a database's transaction log rather than polling the tables. It gives downstream systems the same ordered, durable change feed that the database itself wrote. PostgreSQL Apache Kafka Circuit breaker A pattern that stops calling a dependency once it has failed often enough, and probes it again after a cool-off. It exists to stop a slow failure from turning into a cascading one. Columnar storage Storing values grouped by column rather than by row. Because the values in one column share a type and usually a narrow range, they compress well together — and a query that needs three columns of two hundred reads only three. Avro & Parquet Apache Spark Control plane The part of a distributed system that decides what should happen — the Kubernetes API server, the controllers, the scheduler. It is deliberately separate from the data plane, which does the actual work. Kubernetes CRD — CustomResourceDefinition A Kubernetes extension that adds a new kind of object to the API, so you can model your own domain — and then get controllers, RBAC and the CLI for free. Kubernetes Eventual consistency A guarantee that replicas of the same data converge, but that a read may return a stale value until they do. It buys write throughput and availability at the price of having to reason about what a reader sees. PostgreSQL Idempotency The property of an operation that can be applied several times with the same result as applying it once. Retrying is only safe when the thing being retried is idempotent. Apache Kafka Model Context Protocol Idempotency key A token the client sends with a request so that the server can recognise a repeat of the same operation and return the first result instead of doing the work again. The usual way to make a retry safe. whereq.cloud Immutable infrastructure The practice of never patching a running server, only replacing it. A change is a new image and a new deployment; the old one is drained and discarded, so the running state is always reproducible from the configuration. Docker Kubernetes Kafka partition An ordered slice of a topic. Ordering is guaranteed inside a partition and only inside one; a consumer group owns every partition of a topic, so adding consumers to a group divides the work and adding a group multiplies it. Apache Kafka Leader election How a cluster of peers agrees on which one is currently responsible for a role, so that exactly one of them does the work. It is how a group coordinator, a scheduler or a shard owner avoids two nodes doing the same thing at once. Apache Kafka Kubernetes MVCC — Multi-Version Concurrency Control A concurrency scheme where each transaction reads a consistent snapshot of the data, and updates write new versions rather than overwriting in place. Readers never block writers and writers never block readers — at the cost of having to clean up versions nobody reads any more. PostgreSQL OLAP versus OLTP Two different workloads with two different optimisations. OLTP is the transactional system of record — many small writes, each cheap and durable. OLAP is the analytical system — few large scans over many rows, each touching few columns. A schema tuned for one is usually bad for the other. PostgreSQL Apache Spark Partitioning Splitting a dataset across shards so that work and storage are divided between them. In Kafka it is the unit of parallelism; in a database it is how one very large table is broken into manageable pieces. Apache Kafka PostgreSQL Predicate pushdown Pushing a filter down to where the data is read, so that rows which cannot match are never loaded. In Parquet it works with the statistics in the footer, which lets an engine skip whole row groups. Avro & Parquet Apache Spark Projection pushdown Reading only the columns a query actually needs. It is the single biggest reason a columnar format beats a row format on analytical work: three columns of two hundred is three columns of bytes. Avro & Parquet RAG — Retrieval-Augmented Generation Fetching relevant context before asking a model to answer, and giving it that context in the prompt. It is how a model answers from your data rather than from whatever it happened to learn — and it is why the retrieval step, not the model, is usually the part to get right. whereq.cloud LangChain & LangGraph Rate limiting Capping how much work a caller can ask for in a window. The token bucket is the common shape: tokens are added at a fixed rate and spent per request, so bursts are allowed but the long-run rate is bounded. Reconciliation The loop at the heart of Kubernetes: observe what is, compare it with what should be, and act on the difference. Because it is a loop rather than a procedure, it can run repeatedly, out of order, and recover from a failure in the middle. Kubernetes Row group Parquet's unit of storage: a horizontal slice of rows, itself divided into column chunks and pages. The statistics for each column chunk live in the file footer, which is what makes whole row groups skippable. Avro & Parquet Saga A distributed transaction written as a sequence of local transactions, each with a compensating action that undoes it if a later step fails. There is no single commit; there is an order and a set of compensations. Schema registry The service that holds the schema each topic's records follow, and that checks producers and consumers against it. On this page What it is How it works Under the hood Where to read more AP ReferencesThe Storage Formats Avro & Parquet Two file formats that disagree about how data should be laid out — and why that matters. Visit project Avro & Parquet at a glance Role The Storage Formats Collection The References Shelf Domain Data & Streaming Status Apache top-level projects What it does Parquet — columnar, so a query touching three of two hundred columns reads three. Parquet footer statistics — minimum, maximum and null counts per column chunk. Page indexes and predicate pushdown, so whole row groups can be skipped entirely. Avro — the schema travels with the data, as JSON. Avro schema resolution — explicit writer/reader rules for forward and backward compatibility. See also Apache KafkaReferences Apache SparkReferences PostgreSQLReferences whereq.cloudUniverse Go to Visit project What it is Parquet was created at Twitter and Cloudera and is now the default file format of the lakehouse ecosystem — Iceberg, Delta Lake and Hudi all assume it. It stores values column by column, which means the bytes of a column sit next to each other and can be compressed together. Avro is the other way round. It stores records one at a time, with the schema embedded as JSON, and it was designed around a different problem: a stream of events whose producers and consumers evolve independently. How it works The practical consequence of the layout difference is projection pushdown. A query that needs three columns out of two hundred reads three columns of bytes, not two hundred columns of rows — and because Parquet also keeps per-column-chunk statistics in its footer, an engine can skip whole row groups that cannot match a filter. Columnar writes are the weak side of Parquet: appending one record means touching every column buffer, so writers batch into row groups and small frequent appends are poor. Avro handles small appends well and has explicit rules for resolving a writer's schema against a reader's schema — defaults and type promotions included. Both formats store their schema with the data and both support per-column compression codecs. Parquet added a typed `Variant` representation for heterogeneous values, introduced in August 2025 and documented by Apache in February 2026. Under the hood Parquet Avro Layout Columnar Row-oriented Built for Reading — analytical queries Writing — events and records Schema In the file, as Thrift In the file, as JSON Column pruning Yes — projection and predicate pushdown No Schema evolution Limited on its own; a table format manages it Strong, rule-based writer/reader resolution Small appends Poor Good Typical home The analytical warehouse Kafka payloads and the landing zone Where to read more The Parquet site The Avro site Deep dive into Avro and Parquet formats ← Back to The References Shelf · Next: Docker

On this page What it is How it works Under the hood Where to read more DO ReferencesThe Container Runtime Docker The packaging format almost every service now ships in. Visit project Docker at a glance Role The Container Runtime Collection The References Shelf Domain Platform & Operations Status BuildKit by default What it does A Dockerfile — a declarative recipe for an image. BuildKit, the default builder since the legacy path was deprecated. Buildx — builders that can run as a container, in Kubernetes, or on a remote daemon. Layer caching — only the layers that changed are rebuilt. OCI images — the format Docker images are written in, and the one other runtimes read. See also KubernetesReferences whereq.cloudUniverse Go to Visit project What it is An image is a filesystem plus the metadata needed to run it. A container is that filesystem mounted, with a process started inside it and a handful of kernel features — namespaces, cgroups, capability dropping — keeping it from touching anything it should not. The value was never the packaging format on its own. It was that the packaging format became a contract: the thing that runs in CI is the thing that runs in production, byte for byte. How it works A build is a sequence of layers, each one a diff. The cache is the diff chain, so a build only re-runs the steps after the last thing that changed. BuildKit parallelised that, added better cache control, and made the build itself able to run somewhere other than your machine. BuildKit is the default builder for Docker Desktop and Docker Engine; `docker build` uses Buildx unless you are in Windows container mode or set `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0`. With BuildKit only the files your build actually uses are transmitted, and leading `../` paths are stripped rather than followed. Buildx exposes four drivers: `docker` (the bundled library), `docker-container`, `kubernetes`, and `remote`. Windows container support is the one place the legacy builder is still used, because BuildKit's Windows support is still experimental. On this page What it is How it works Under the hood Where to read more AK ReferencesThe Event Log Apache Kafka A distributed, append-only log that every service can read from. Visit project Apache Kafka at a glance Role The Event Log Collection The References Shelf Domain Data & Streaming Status v4.4.0 What it does Partitions — the unit of both parallelism and ordering. Consumer groups, so a set of consumers shares the work of a topic. Replication across brokers, tracked by the in-sync replica set. KRaft consensus — since 4.0 there is no ZooKeeper, and the metadata quorum is part of Kafka itself. Exactly-once transactions, with read-process-write semantics. See also whereq.cloudUniverse Apache SparkReferences Avro & ParquetReferences KubernetesReferences Go to Visit project What it is A queue moves a message from a producer to a consumer. A log keeps the message, in order, for as long as you like, and lets every consumer decide for itself where to read. That difference is the whole design, and it is what lets you replay history, add a new consumer without touching the old one, and decouple the pace of production from the pace of consumption. How it works A topic is split into partitions, and a partition is an ordered sequence. Each consumer group owns every partition of a topic, so adding consumers to a group divides the work, while adding a new group multiplies it. Ordering is guaranteed within a partition and only within a partition. Kafka 4.4.0 was released on October 22, 2026. Kafka 4.0, in March 2025, removed ZooKeeper mode entirely and made KRaft the default — the metadata quorum lives in the cluster rather than in a separate ensemble. KIP-848's new consumer group protocol reached general availability in 4.0, moving rebalance complexity into the broker's group coordinator. Clients and Kafka Streams require Java 11; brokers, Connect and the tools require Java 17. Visit project Kubernetes at a glance Role The Orchestrator Collection The References Shelf Domain Platform & Operations Status v1.37.x What it does Declarative desired state — you declare what should exist, not how to create it. A control plane whose controllers continuously reconcile actual state against desired state. A scheduler that places workloads by resource requests and constraints. Rolling updates with health checks and automatic rollback. CRDs — extend the API with your own kinds. See also DockerReferences Apache SparkReferences whereq.cloudUniverse Go to Visit project What it is The idea that makes Kubernetes work is the reconcile loop. You state what should be true; a controller observes what is true, computes the difference, and acts. It is a loop, not a procedure, so it does not need to run once, in order, or perfectly. Everything else — the scheduler, the self-healing, the rolling update, the service discovery — falls out of that loop applied to different kinds of object. How it works A Deployment says "run three of these". The controller notices the mismatch between three and the two that are running, and creates one. The scheduler finds a node with room. When that node dies, the replacement goes elsewhere and the pod's identity moves with it — which is what a StatefulSet adds on top. The project maintains release branches for the three most recent minor releases: 1.37, 1.36 and 1.35. The latest patch on the 1.37 branch is 1.37.2, released in October 2026; 1.38 is in beta. Minor releases land three times a year on roughly fifteen-week cycles, and deprecated APIs may be removed with a minor release. On this page What it is How it works Under the hood Where to read more LL ReferencesThe Agent Framework LangChain & LangGraph The standard way to build something that reasons, calls tools and remembers. Visit project LangChain & LangGraph at a glance Role The Agent Framework Collection The References Shelf Domain AI & Agents Status langchain 1.5.0 What it does `create_agent` — the standard entry point, built on LangGraph. Persistence — conversations checkpoint and survive across sessions. Streaming of tokens, tool calls and reasoning traces in real time. Human-in-the-loop — pause an agent for approval before a sensitive action. Time travel — rewind a conversation and explore an alternate path. Middleware for model routing, retries, summarisation and policy. See also Model Context ProtocolReferences OllamaReferences whereq.cloudUniverse Go to Visit project What it is An agent is a loop: think, choose a tool, run it, feed the result back, decide again. LangChain is the set of building blocks for that loop, and LangGraph is the engine that runs it — a graph of nodes with explicit edges, where every step can be checkpointed, retried or interrupted. The v1 line deliberately narrowed the surface. `create_agent` is now the standard way to build an agent, and it replaces the older prebuilt React agent; the long tail of legacy functionality moved into `langchain-classic` rather than being deleted. How it works Because `create_agent` runs on LangGraph, an agent gets persistence, streaming, human-in-the-loop and time travel without any extra wiring. A conversation is checkpointed as it goes, so a restart resumes where it left off and a human can approve a step before it happens. LangChain 1.5 adds decision models and decision-driven middleware — typed, probabilistic answers about text, messages and structured state. Model routing middleware selects a model per run from the configured choices. LangGraph 1.2 adds per-node timeouts, a `DeltaChannel` that stores only the incremental change per step, and a content-block streaming protocol with typed per-channel projections. Python 3.11 is the floor: LangChain 1.5 and langchain-core 1.8 dropped Python 3.10. On this page What it is How it works Under the hood Where to read more MC ReferencesThe Agent Protocol Model Context Protocol An open standard for connecting AI applications to tools and data. Visit project Model Context Protocol at a glance Role The Agent Protocol Collection The References Shelf Domain AI & Agents Status Specification 2026-07-28 What it does One message format — JSON-RPC 2.0 — carried identically over every transport. Two standard transports: stdio for a local subprocess, Streamable HTTP for a remote server. Three primitives — tools, resources and prompts — plus an optional discovery call for capabilities. Tier 1 SDKs for TypeScript, Python, Go and C#, with Rust in beta. A formal extensions framework, so proposals can mature outside the core. See also whereq.cloudUniverse LangChain & LangGraphReferences OllamaReferences Go to Visit project What it is An assistant that cannot call anything is a text box. MCP is the answer to the awkward half of that sentence: it gives a model a standard way to reach the outside world, and it gives the outside world a standard way to describe what it offers. The protocol is deliberately small. A server advertises tools (functions a model may call), resources (data a model may read) and prompts (reusable interaction templates). A client discovers them, calls them, and handles the results. Everything else — how the two are connected — is a transport detail. How it works The 2026-07-28 revision changed the protocol's core from a bidirectional, stateful conversation into a stateless request/response one. Every request is self-describing, so any request can land on any instance behind a plain round-robin load balancer, with no shared session store to run. Two transports carry the messages. On stdio, the client launches the server as a subprocess and exchanges newline-delimited JSON-RPC over its standard streams; the server may log freely to stderr, but stdout must carry nothing but protocol messages. On Streamable HTTP, the server exposes one endpoint that accepts POST, and answers each request with either a JSON object or a Server-Sent Events stream scoped to that request. Every Streamable HTTP request must carry an `MCP-Protocol-Version` header that matches the version in the body's `_meta`; a mismatch is rejected with a 400. The `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` headers carry the method and tool names, so a gateway can route, rate-limit and authorise without parsing the JSON body. Server-to-client calls such as sampling and elicitation are now expressed as Multi Round-Trip Requests — the answer is carried back inside a result rather than needing a permanently open stream. List responses carry cache hints and a deterministic order, so a client can cache a tool catalogue and keep an upstream prompt cache stable across reconnects. On this page What it is How it works Under the hood Where to read more OL ReferencesThe Local Model Runner Ollama Run a large language model on your own machine, behind one HTTP API. Visit project Ollama at a glance Role The Local Model Runner Collection The References Shelf Domain AI & Agents Status v0.12.6 What it does One command to fetch and run a model — `ollama pull`, then `ollama run`. You install one binary, name a model, and it is running. The model library is a registry of tagged builds — `llama3.2`, `mistral`, `gemma4` and so on — each of which bundles the weights with everything needed to run them. That is what makes the same call work against a local server and against Ollama's hosted models. How it works The local server binds to 127.0.0.1 on port 11434 by default; `OLLAMA_HOST` moves it. On this page What it is How it works Under the hood Where to read more PO ReferencesThe Database PostgreSQL The relational database that most of the world runs on. Visit project PostgreSQL at a glance Role The Database Collection The References Shelf Domain Data & Streaming Status PostgreSQL 19 What it does Full ACID transactions. MVCC — readers never block writers, and writers never block readers. A cost-based query planner, with statistics it keeps up to date itself. Row-level security, so a database can enforce tenancy on its own. Extensions — PostGIS for geography, pgvector for embeddings. See also whereq.cloudUniverse caijing.todayUniverse Apache KafkaReferences Apache SparkReferences Go to Visit project What it is PostgreSQL is what "a database" means when someone says it without qualifying. It is a full relational system with transactions, foreign keys, check constraints, views and a planner that will rewrite your query if it thinks it can do better. The extensions are what turned it from a good default into an unusually capable one. PostGIS makes it a spatial database; pgvector makes it a vector store; the JSON operators make it a document store that still keeps its constraints. How it works Every update rewrites the row, and every old version stays visible to readers until no one needs it. That is MVCC, and it is why a reporting query does not block the write that is landing next to it — and why the vacuum process exists to clean up what nobody reads any more. PostgreSQL 19 was released on November 19, 2026. PostgreSQL 18, released September 2025, added an asynchronous I/O subsystem, `uuidv7()`, skip-scan B-tree lookups, virtual generated columns by default, OAuth authentication, and `OLD`/`NEW` in `RETURNING`. MD5 password authentication is deprecated as of 18, and will be removed in a future major release. On this page What it is How it works Under the hood Where to read more AS ReferencesThe Compute Engine Apache Spark The engine for computing over data too large to fit on one machine. Visit project Apache Spark at a glance Role The Compute Engine Collection The References Shelf Domain Data & Streaming Status v4.3.0 What it does The DataFrame API — SQL-shaped operations over distributed data. The Catalyst optimizer and the Tungsten execution engine. Structured Streaming — the same API over a continuous stream. Connectors for Parquet, ORC, Avro, JDBC, Kafka and Delta Lake. Runs on Kubernetes, YARN and standalone clusters. See also Apache KafkaReferences Avro & ParquetReferences PostgreSQLReferences KubernetesReferences Go to Visit project What it is Spark began as a way to do MapReduce-style computation in memory instead of writing every intermediate result to disk. It has since grown into a general query engine with a SQL front end, a streaming subsystem and a machine-learning library, all sharing one execution core. How it works You write transformations; the engine writes the job. Catalyst pushes filters and projections down into the source, the Tungsten engine compiles whole stages into generated code, and the scheduler inserts shuffle boundaries where data has to be redistributed between partitions. Visit project TypeScript at a glance Role The Type System Collection The References Shelf Domain Web & Interface Status v7.0.2 What it does Structural typing — shapes, not names, so the type follows the data. Inference from context, so the common case needs no annotation at all. Declaration files, so a library can ship its own types. Gradual adoption — a `.js` file can be renamed `.ts` one at a time. A native compiler — TypeScript 7 is a Go port, roughly ten times faster. See also ReactReferences DocusaurusReferences whereq.github.ioUniverse whereq.cloudUniverse Go to Visit project What it is The point of a type system is not to describe what the code does. It is to make the set of things the code can do explicit, so a mistake is caught by a program that never runs the code at all. TypeScript does that without asking you to change how JavaScript works. Types are erased at compile time, the output is ordinary JavaScript, and every tool that already understands JavaScript still understands the result. How it works The compiler walks the program, assigns a type to every expression, and reports the ones that cannot be reconciled. Because the type system is structural, two types match when their shapes match — which is why a plain object literal is often accepted where a class instance was expected, and why an interface is a description rather than a constructor. TypeScript 6.0 was released in March 2026, and TypeScript 7.0 followed in July — a native Go port, roughly ten times faster on large projects. TypeScript 7.0.2 is the current release; 7.1 is in beta. Declaration files (`.d.ts`) let a library publish its own types, so consumers get the same checking without writing anything. The applications above it read from that contract instead of building their own. That is the whole idea. A market-news desk, a freight platform, a tutoring companion and a photo vault are not four unrelated products that happen to share a name — they are four readers of the same database, each one shaped around a different question a person actually asks. How the universe fits together It divides into three layers. The foundation — the data platform (whereq.cloud), the identity layer (keytomarvel.com), the research station (whereq.ca), and this site, the universe's public voice. The engines — the spatial engine (whereq.com) and the temporal engine (chroniq.cc), which own geography and time respectively. The products — flowdesk.top, caijing.today, qhaul.ca, catobigato.com, whereq.cc, whereq-dosbox and ccbus.cc: each one a finished thing a person can open and use. The layering is what keeps the universe honest. A product can change its interface without anyone touching the data, and the data can be corrected once, everywhere, without shipping six patches.
