documents.t: 鼠标是最有意思的一个，也是这个移植版改动最多的一个。 INT 33h 是一个对 AX 的 switch，实现了 35 个功能码。这里真正要紧的是两个：AX=03h，返回光标位置和按键状态；AX=0Ch，登记游戏自己的事件回调。 关于 AX=03h，有一点是我读到代码才真正明白的。mouse.buttons 是一个电平，不是边沿。Mouse_ButtonPressed() 置位，Mouse_ButtonReleased() 清位，AX=03h 把这个掩码原样交回去： case 0x03: /* Return Position and Button Status */ reg_bx=mouse.buttons; reg_cx=POS_X; reg_dx=POS_Y; break; 每帧轮询 AX=03h 的游戏，问的是「这个按钮现在按着吗」，而不是「刚才有没有点一下」。 就这一个事实，决定了整个触摸层的设计。
documents.s: INT 33h，以及为什么「点击」必须是「按住」
documents.h: #int-33h以及为什么点击必须是按住

documents.t: 这个移植版的第一版做法很直白：手指按下就是 press，手指抬起就是 release，敲一下算一次点击。 这是错的。而且错在一种只有游戏才会暴露的地方。三国志英杰传的战斗界面读的是实时按键状态。如果按下和抬起落在它两次轮询之间，游戏根本看不见这次点击。光标动了，敲击等于没发生，玩家只会觉得这个应用坏了。 所以现在手指在玻璃上按多久，按钮就按住多久： SDL_FINGERDOWN → Mouse_ButtonPressed(0) // 左键，按住 SDL_FINGERMOTION → 移动光标，按键仍然按着 SDL_FINGERUP → Mouse_ButtonReleased(0) 敲一下于是变成一次真正的「按住再松开」的点击。拖动也变成真正的拖动——因为光标是在按键按着的时候移动的。 画面两侧的两块键盘区。整块屏幕就是那只鼠标。
documents.s: 从一根手指到一只 DOS 鼠标

documents.t: 还有第二个 bug，而且更古怪。DOSBox 在全屏时会「捕获鼠标」，这会置上 sdl.mouse.locked。这个标志一置上，Mouse_CursorMoved() 就忽略绝对位置，只累加相对位移。 在桌面上这是对的——被捕获的鼠标本来就是相对设备。可手机上根本没有鼠标可捕获，后果就是每一次敲击都被忽略，光标卡在屏幕正中。 修之前和修之后的实测： 点 (700, 300) 点 (1500, 800) 点 (1000, 500) 之前 320, 100 320, 100 320, 100 之后 97, 55 453, 148 231, 92 数字是精确的：0.153 × 80 × 8 = 97——DOS 文本屏 80 × 25 个字符格，每格 8 像素。原本永远落在同一个错误格子上的点击，现在落在你真正按下的地方。
documents.s: 吞掉每一次点击的那个陷阱
documents.h: #吞掉每一次点击的那个陷阱

documents.t: DOS 鼠标有两个按钮，触摸屏只有一个。而绝大多数 DOS 游戏里右键是取消或返回，所以丢掉右键就是丢掉了一整类交互。 这里没有长按手势，也没有上下文菜单。右键由两个机制送出，而且两个都是按住式按钮，和左键完全一样： 画面上的第二根手指。左键会先松开，所以两个按钮不会重叠；右键一直按到那根手指抬起。 屏幕上的 RMB 键，在左边那块、紧挨 Tab。它通过 JNI 桥往 DOSBox 的事件队列里推一个真正的 SDL_BUTTON_RIGHT 的 SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN，事件走的路径和普通鼠标点击一模一样。 第二个机制有意思的地方在于，它压根不是一个手势——它是另一个事件类型，被塞进模拟器本来就在读的那个队列。

这是我把存档格式重写了两次的那个 bug 的根子。 INT 33h 驱动的状态住在一个宿主的文件内静态结构体里，不在模拟出来的内存中。其中有三样东西，来宾在读档之后没法自己重建： 游戏用 AX=0Ch 登记的事件回调——段、偏移和事件掩码； AX=09h 定义的图形光标和它的热点； 光标范围、位置、可见性和灵敏度。 少了第一样，症状精确得让人难受：光标还在动——那是 DOSBox 在画——但游戏的点击送不到游戏里。对话框的确认按钮就是没反应。模拟器看起来活蹦乱跳，游戏却是聋的。 少了第二样，光标退回默认的白色方块、热点归零，于是看得见的光标和真正的点击点对不上，敲击会落在目标的偏上偏左。 所以鼠标驱动必须成为存档的一部分。第一次尝试存了整个结构体。 结果把游戏卡死了。 三国志英杰传在读档时挂起，而且过一分钟就再也不响应点击——事件队列在一个卡住的 in_UIR 标志后面堆满了。把过期的队列和过期的 in_UIR 喂回中断处理程序，就是把垃圾喂给了游戏自己的回调。 修法是搞懂两种状态的分别： 配置值得保存，运行期状态是毒药。 最终形态存的是一个专门的 MouseStateBlock，只放来宾重建不了的东西——回调三元组、光标范围与位置、热点、光标掩码、灵敏度。读档时则把所有易失的部分重置：事件队列、按键与点击计数器、重入标志、光标绘制的背景缓冲。 还有一条规则，这是「宿主指针」规则的小号版本：结构体里有两个指向光标位图的宿主指针。它们从不写进文件，而是在读档后根据保存的光标类型重新推导：用户自定义的图形光标用恢复出来的掩码，其余一律用内置箭头。
documents.s: 驱动的状态住在来宾内存之外
documents.h: #驱动的状态住在来宾内存之外

documents.t: 中断控制器是同一个形状的问题，而这个移植版得出了同一个答案。 存档是机器的快照，而机器包含它的中断子系统。PIC_SaveState 和 PIC_LoadState 会把两个控制器结构体写进去——然后加载器故意不把全部都恢复： /* Keep the game's interrupt MASK and configuration, but drop any stale * pending/in-service state: a restored in-service bit would block all * lower-priority IRQs (so the RTC that drives INT 15h/86h, and thus sound * timing, would stall), and a stale request bit would fire a spurious IRQ. * At the top-of-main-loop restore point no IRQ is genuinely mid-service. */ pics[i].imrr = ~pics[i].imr; pics[i].irr = 0; pics[i].isr = 0; 掩码是配置——来宾自己决定要哪些中断，它要留下来。在服务位和请求位是瞬态——一个残留的在服务位会卡死整个优先级链，一个残留的请求位会打出一次莫名的中断。 保留配置，丢掉运行期状态。同一句话，在两个不同的子系统里说了两遍，而两次都是靠撞墙撞出来的。 格式版本也随着设计在动：8 是「整个鼠标驱动状态」，9 是「精简成回调 + 范围 + 位置」，10 是「光标形状、热点和其余配置」。含义变了的格式必须把版本号喊出来，这样旧的存档会被拒绝，而不是被误读。

这个答案更让人意外，也更值得直说：BIOS 中断层是上游代码。 src/ints/ 下的每一个文件自导入以来都没动过，只有一个例外。mouse.cpp 有五个导入之后的提交；而 int10.cpp 及其八个兄弟、bios.cpp、bios_disk.cpp、bios_keyboard.cpp、ems.cpp、xms.cpp 一个都没有。 DOS 层也一样。src/dos/dos.cpp——整个 INT 21h 处理程序——以及 dos_misc.cpp、dos_classes.cpp、dos_memory.cpp 与导入的源码逐字节相同。这个移植版对它的唯一侵入是一行，而且和中断没有关系： SegSet16(ds,pspseg);SegSet16(es,pspseg); /* WhereQ: a guest program has taken over the machine, so the boot * is over and a save-state request may be serviced. The shell * itself never reaches its prompt in this case (it is blocked * inside the program it started), so this is the only place where * the save-state module learns that the guest is running. */ SAVESTATE_GuestReady(); 连包启动器都是走的标准路径。每个游戏会生成一个 RUN.BAT，被追加到模拟器的 [autoexec] 里；来宾随后用 INT 21h AH=4Bh 去 exec 它，再 AH=4Bh 跑游戏自己的 PLAY.BAT，最后 AH=4Ch 退出。这个移植版没有新增任何启动器 API——它只是挑了一个文件名，剩下的交给 DOS。 整个移植版大致就是这个形状：真正有意思的工作几乎从不在 BIOS 层，而在它上面那一层——把一根手指变成一只鼠标，把一次轻触变成一个按住不松的按钮，把一个游戏变成存档能带走的东西。
documents.s: 这个移植版没有改的东西

documents.t: 看这一层工作，最省事的办法是打开 MOUSE 日志分组，在 dosbox.conf 里： [log] logfile=/sdcard/dosbox.log mouse=true Android 应用不带 [log] 段，所以默认是关的。打开之后，驱动没有实现的每一次 INT 33h 调用都会被报出来： Mouse Function 0018 not implemented! 这等于直接读出了游戏在要什么、驱动又没回答什么。再往前一个函数的地方，有一行被注释掉的日志，会打印每一次 INT 33h 调用的 AX、BX、CX 和光标位置——对想读这份代码的人来说，这是这个树里最值得解开的一行。 👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox——源码、完整的中断地图 docs/INTERRUPTS.md，以及背后的技术参考。

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。 DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。 这个移植版基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。 DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植版与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。 模拟器就是一台由「对还没人问过的问题的回答」造出来的机器。真正有意思的工作，在于决定那个问题从一根拇指上传来时，回答应该是什么。

Here is a thing I noticed while I was testing the app on my own phone. Every DOSBox guide I have ever read was written by somebody who already knew what a .zip bundle was. They start at the interesting part — the sound chips, the save-state format, the JIT — and assume you have been running DOS since 1994. That assumption is wrong for most people holding a phone. The hardest part of putting an old game on a modern phone is not the emulator. It is the first five minutes: getting the game onto the phone at all, in a shape the app can start. So I wrote the guide I wanted instead. Seven steps, one screenshot of every screen, and no assumption that you have ever seen a command prompt.
documents.s: The guide I wanted and could not find

documents.t: Install the app. The APK is on the releases page. Open it. You land on the Files panel, and it is empty. Press + Install a bundle (.zip) and pick a .zip game file. Press Play. The game starts. Press File (top left) whenever you want to come back to the list. That is the whole thing. Everything below is the detail behind those five steps — read it if you want to understand what you are doing, skip it if you just want to play.

Phone Android 5.0 or newer, any phone or tablet Space about 60 MB for the app, plus the size of the game Network none needed once the app and the game are on the phone Account none You also need a game, as a single .zip file. A game for this app is not the same thing as a ZIP of your own files — see Where do I get a game? below.

The app is not in the source repository. It is built by the release pipeline and published on the releases page as whereq-dosbox-<version>.apk, with a .sha256 file next to it carrying the checksum. Copy the .apk to your phone — cable, cloud drive, a file-sharing app, whatever is at hand — then tap it on the phone. Android asks whether to allow installing from that app; allow it, and the install goes through. The app appears on your home screen as the >_ mark: The WhereQ-DOSBox icon on the home screen. The name in the app list, the notification, and the screen Android shows for the app all read WhereQ-DOSBox: The Android App info page for WhereQ-DOSBox.

Open the app. You land in the Files panel — the screen that lists what you have installed: The Files panel on a fresh install, with no games yet. Two ways to get a game in, both at the top of the panel: button what it does + Install a bundle (.zip) pick one .zip from your phone Install all bundles from a folder unpack every .zip in one folder at once Press + Install a bundle (.zip), and the system's file picker opens. Pick your game's .zip — usually in Downloads — and the app unpacks it and registers it. The panel then lists it: The Files panel with two games installed. Each game in the list has four buttons: button what it does Play start the game from the beginning States save and load save states for this game Launch… run a different program, or add driver files, before the game Remove uninstall this game from the app

A game for this app is a .zip with a small, fixed shape: the bundle ───────── PLAY.BAT the entry point - the app runs this <the game files> whatever the game needs __meta.json the name the app shows in the list That is it. The repository ships one, so you can see the shape and try the app immediately: examples/game-bundle — the STARFALL demo. Copy whereq-demo-bundle.zip from that folder to your phone and install it. For real games: sites that still host abandonware DOS games generally offer them as a .zip. If a game's archive contains the game files but no PLAY.BAT, the app cannot start it — make a PLAY.BAT that runs the game's executable, and zip the folder again.
documents.s: Where do I get a game?

documents.t: Press Play. The emulator restarts the app and boots the game, and you land at a DOS prompt: The DOSBox welcome banner and the C:\> prompt, with the two keyboard pads beside the picture. Type the game's name and press Enter. From then on it is the real game — the real keyboard, the real sound, the real mouse. Here is a real 1994 DOS game running on a phone: Formula 1 (Domark, 1994) running on the phone, with the on-screen keyboard around it. And here is the STARFALL demo: The STARFALL title screen. STARFALL being played, with the two keyboard pads beside the picture. The first time a game runs, Android may ask whether the app may send you notifications. It uses them for a "back to the game" reminder when you leave the app. Answer either way — declining only means you lose that reminder: The Android notification permission prompt. When a game is running, the File key (top left) brings the Files panel back over it, and the panel shows a Resume line for the game that is running right now: The Files panel over a running game, with Resume F1 above the list.

There is no physical keyboard in the way, because the screen keyboard is the keyboard. In landscape you get two pads beside the picture, the way a handheld console is built: the left pad has the arrow keys as a D-pad and the left half of a split QWERTY, the right pad has the action keys (Alt, Ctrl, Shift, Space, Enter) and the right half of the alphabet. Two keys change what the pads show: key shows #+= the punctuation layer Fn F1–F12, Ins/Del, Home/End, PgUp/PgDn, Caps, PrtSc, Pause The switched key lights up while its layer is on. The #+= layer — the punctuation sits where the letters were. The Fn layer — the whole F-row and the editing keys, without stealing a single key from the letters. Modifiers work two ways. Tap Ctrl, Alt or Shift and it stays armed for the next key — Ctrl, then C. Hold it and it behaves like a real key for as long as your finger is down, which is what a game expects of its fire and strafe keys while the other thumb steers. The mouse is the screen. Your finger is the mouse: drag to move the pointer, tap to click, and the on-screen RMB key (on the left pad, next to Tab) is the right mouse button — in most DOS games that is cancel or back. A second finger on the picture does the same, at that finger's own position. Turn the phone to portrait and the pads fold into a single strip along the bottom, for the games that are taller than they are wide. The layout follows the screen. The letterbox bar beside the 4:3 DOS picture has to be at least 116 dp wide to carry a full pad. On a narrow landscape phone it still does — an 18:9 bar is 137 dp — but the letter keys are squeezed to about 24 dp, against 33 dp on a 20:9 screen. The D-pad and the action keys keep their full size; it is the letters that get tight. The #+= and Fn layers are tight in the same way. The same layout on an 18:9 screen. The pads still fit, but the letters are tight — about 24 dp wide, against 33 dp on a 20:9 one. Below 116 dp the pads give way to columns. There is no longer room for a half-keyboard beside the picture, so the pads become a single column of keys per side — arrows on the left, the action keys on the right — and the whole QWERTY folds up from the bottom when you want it. The columns layout — one column of keys per side, and the DOS picture keeps the middle. The ⌨ key in the left column opens the QWERTY, which rises from the bottom over the picture and closes again with the same key. The same layout with the QWERTY folded up from the bottom. The keyboard icon is lit, and tapping it again puts it away. Below 56 dp even that is too much, and the keyboard becomes a slim strip along the bottom of the screen.
documents.s: Step 4 — The keyboard and the mouse

documents.t: Some games want a gamepad, not a typewriter. Game Mode replaces the keyboard pads with a console-style controller: a direction pad and a trackball, with the buttons a DOS game actually fires, jumps and strafes with. Game Mode. The letter pads are gone; a D-pad and a trackball take their place, in the same two bars. Getting in and out is a nod to the old days. With the keyboard pads showing, switch Caps Lock on first — double-tap Shift, and the key turns blue and reads CAPS — then enter the Konami code on the pads — ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A — and the pads flip into Game Mode. The B and A must be capital: the code watches the letters in the case you actually type them, so a lowercase "ba" just types "ba" into the DOS prompt. To go back, enter it again on the gamepad: the ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → on the D-pad, then X, Y (the two face buttons stand in for B and A). The phone's Back button also returns you to the keyboard. The gold button at the top-left names the current profile; tap it to cycle, long-press for a picker. Each game remembers the profile and D-pad you last used with it. Long-press the gold profile button and the picker opens — the three profiles, and the way into the remap screen. profile left thumb right thumb for Hybrid (default) 8-way D-pad trackball games that mix keys and mouse — Dune II, X-COM, Doom with a mouse Action 8-way D-pad FIRE / JUMP / USE / ENT buttons keyboard arcade/shooters — Wolf3D, Keen, Prince of Persia Point big LEFT / RIGHT mouse buttons trackball mouse-only games — Monkey Island, Civilization, Lemmings The Action profile: FIRE, JUMP, USE and ENT, for the games that fire and jump on the keyboard. The Point & click profile: the mouse buttons take the whole left pad, the trackball the right one. The trackball moves the pointer the way a laptop touchpad does — stroke to move, tap to click — rather than jumping it to where you touch. In Hybrid, holding L-CLICK (left shoulder) while you roll the trackball is a drag-select.
documents.s: Game Mode — a gamepad for action games

documents.t: DOS games don't agree on which keys "up" is. The ARROWS button under the D-pad cycles what the pad sends, and the app remembers your choice per game: mode up / down / left / right a diagonal (e.g. up-right) choose it for ARROWS the arrow keys ↑ ↓ ← → two keys at once (↑ + →) most games — anything that reads the cursor keys NUMPAD the numeric keypad 8 / 2 / 4 / 6 a single key — 7 / 9 / 1 / 3 games built for the numpad, where a diagonal is its own key (many roguelikes and joystick-via-keypad games) WASD the letters W / A / S / D two keys at once (W + D) later shooters and anything mapped to WASD So the difference is both which keys the pad presses and how a diagonal is sent: ARROWS and WASD press the two neighbouring keys together, while NUMPAD has a real key for each of the eight directions. If your game ignores the D-pad, it is almost always the wrong mode — switch with the ARROWS button until it responds.
documents.s: The D-pad output — ARROWS, NUMPAD, WASD

documents.t: Sometimes a game wants a key the pad does not have — F to fire, SPACE to jump, the numeric keypad to shoot. You can teach any Game Mode button to send a different key, and the app remembers it for that game. Long-press the gold profile button (top-left, the one that names the profile) and choose Remap buttons…. The screen enters remap mode: a banner along the top says "Tap a button to remap", and the buttons you can change are outlined in gold. Tap one and a list of keys opens — pick the one you want. DONE (or the banner) leaves remap mode. Remap mode: the gold outline marks the buttons you can change; on the gold FIRE button it has to be dark brown, or it would disappear. you can change you cannot change CTRL, ALT, SHIFT, TAB, STR ◂, STR ▸, SPACE, ENT, USE, JUMP and FIRE the X and Y buttons (they answer the game's Quit? (Y/N) prompts and the Konami code), ESC, the D-pad, the trackball, the mouse buttons, and the function chips (ARROWS, Fn, 1–9, TURBO, SPEED, DRAG, DBL) A changed button shows the new key instead of its old name — FIRE keeps its name and shows the key under it. Reset to default, the first entry in the list, puts the button back. Remaps are per game and cover every profile, so a game remembers what each button sends whichever profile you play it in.

A save state is the whole machine frozen: the CPU, the memory, the video memory, the sound chips, the open DOS file handles. Load it and the game is exactly where you left it — even if the app was closed in between. Press File, then States next to the game: The Save states sheet, with three empty slots. There are three slots. Press Save to freeze the game into slot 1, and the sheet shows when you did it: The sheet with a saved slot — Slot 1, two minutes ago. Close the sheet and the Files panel carries a Resume line for the game, naming the slot and the moment it was made: The Files panel with Resume starfall-v2 · slot 1 · just now. Load puts the game back. A slot survives quitting the app and rebooting the phone.

A save state normally lives inside the app's own private storage. Android deletes that when you uninstall the app — and when you lose the phone, or switch phones. Your games and your saves go with it. So the app asks, once, whether you want a second copy somewhere that is yours: The Keep your saves safe prompt, after the first save. The app says the same thing in its own dialog, which you can open at any time: The Saves folder dialog, with no folder set yet. Press Choose folder, and the system asks you to allow the app into a folder on your phone: The system permission dialog for the folder. Pick a folder, press USE THIS FOLDER, and press ALLOW. From then on every slot is mirrored into that folder, compressed, next to the game itself. You can see, and change, the folder at any time under Config → Saves folder: The Settings dialog. The Saves folder dialog, with a folder set. Two notes: Android refuses to let an app take the Download folder itself, because that would be too broad a permission. Pick any other folder — Documents is fine. You only have to answer this once. The app does not ask again.

This is what the folder is for. Uninstall the app, install it again, and choose the same folder. The app looks inside it and finds your games — they are still there, because they were never inside the app: The folder on the phone after the app was uninstalled. The app notices the games that are not installed and offers to bring them back: The Restore games prompt. Press Restore, and they come back with their names and their saves: Restored two games, with their saves ready. And the save state still knows when it was made: The restored slot, still saying three minutes ago. That last line is the point of the whole feature. A save that was made three minutes ago says three minutes ago, even after it was rebuilt from the folder on a fresh install.
documents.s: Step 7 — After a reinstall, or on a new phone

documents.t: inside the app the folder you picked ──────────── ─────────────────── the games <your folder>/ the save-state slots <game name>/ slot1.gz slot2.gz bundle.zip gone when the app is removed stays until you delete it

what you see what it means what to do "That save file is damaged" the slot was written by an older version the save format grew a version; older slots are refused rather than misread. Start a new slot. The game does not start the bundle has no PLAY.BAT, or the entry point is wrong open the .zip and check that PLAY.BAT runs the game's executable Nothing happens when you tap Play the emulator is restarting to boot the game wait a few seconds — the process restarts on purpose, and the game starts in the new process The keyboard is in the way the pads take the sides of the screen turn the phone to portrait for a single strip along the bottom The mouse does not click the game wants the mouse held drag for movement; the on-screen RMB key, or a second finger on the picture, is the right button You cannot pick the Download folder Android will not grant an app the whole Download folder pick another folder, such as Documents You get a notification prompt the app wants to show the "back to the game" notification allow it or decline it — you can decline, you just lose that notification The game is slow the emulator runs the original hardware, not a fast one it is what the 1994 machine did. It is not the phone being slow.

This post is the guide. The repository holds the same document, plus everything behind it: 👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox — the source, the example bundle, the issues, and the guide itself at docs/USER-GUIDE.md. The technical reference is the long one — how the native build works, how the save-state machine takes a snapshot of the whole machine, the exact FM snapshot, the bundle launcher, the on-screen keyboard, the build pipeline. It is written for engineers, not for phone holders. The releases page carries the APK and its checksum.

None of this is possible without the DOSBox project. DOSBox was written by the DOSBox Team — a volunteer crew who took an operating system from 1994 and made it runnable on every machine the world has produced since, including the ones that did not exist yet. They kept it alive for three decades and gave it away to anyone who wanted it. WhereQ-DOSBox is a thin layer on top of their work. The originality, the craft and the generosity are entirely theirs. This port is built on Em-DOSBox, the Emscripten build of DOSBox r4305 by Boris Gjenero, which grew out of Ismail Khatib's first attempt to compile DOSBox with Emscripten, and rode on the Emscripten work of Alon Zakai. The SDL2 library by Sam Lantinga carries the window, the audio and the touch input. DOSBox is a trademark of the DOSBox project; this port is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DOSBox team. Every screenshot above is a real phone, running the release-signed APK. Nothing here is a mock-up.

在自己的手机上试用这个应用时，我注意到一件事：我读过的每一份 DOSBox 指南，作者都默认你已经知道 .zip 包是什么。他们直接从有意思的部分讲起——声音芯片、存档格式、JIT——然后假定你从 1994 年起就一直在用 DOS。 对大多数拿着手机的人来说，这个假定是错的。把老游戏搬上现代手机，难的从来不是模拟器，而是最初那五分钟：怎么把游戏弄进手机，而且是应用能启动的形状。 所以我干脆写了一份我想要的那一份。七个步骤，每一步都配一张真机截图，不假设你见过命令行。
documents.s: 一份我想要却找不到的指南
documents.h: #一份我想要却找不到的指南

documents.t: 安装应用（APK 在发布页）。 打开它，落到 Files 面板，里面是空的。 按 + Install a bundle (.zip)，选一个 .zip 游戏文件。 按 Play，游戏就开始了。 随时按左上角的 File 回到列表。 就这么多。下面全是这五步背后的细节——想弄明白在做什么就读，想直接玩就跳过。
手机 Android 5.0 及以上，手机平板都行 空间 应用大约 60 MB，再加上游戏本身的大小 网络 应用和游戏都在手机上之后，不需要网络 账号 不需要 你还需要一个游戏，单个 .zip 文件。这里说的「游戏」不是把你自己的文件打个 ZIP——往下看游戏从哪来？。

应用不在源码仓库里。它由发布流水线构建，发布在发布页上，文件名是 whereq-dosbox-<version>.apk，旁边还有一个 .sha256 文件写着校验和。 把 .apk 拷到手机上——数据线、云盘、文件传输，随你——然后在手机上点它。Android 会问要不要允许这个应用安装，允许就行。 应用会出现在你的主屏幕上，就是那个 >_ 标记： 主屏幕上的 WhereQ-DOSBox 图标。 应用列表里的名字、通知里的名字、Android 展示应用信息时写的名字，都写着 WhereQ-DOSBox： WhereQ-DOSBox 的 Android 应用信息页。
documents.s: 第 1 步 —— 安装应用

documents.t: 打开应用。你会落到 Files 面板——列出已安装内容的那个界面： 全新安装后空白的 Files 面板。 两种把游戏放进去的办法，都在面板顶部： 按钮 作用 + Install a bundle (.zip) 从手机里选一个 .zip Install all bundles from a folder 把某一个文件夹里的所有 .zip 一次解开 按 + Install a bundle (.zip)，系统的文件选择器会打开。选你的游戏 .zip——通常在 Downloads 里——应用会解开它并登记好。面板上就列出它了： Files 面板里有两个已安装的游戏。 列表里每个游戏有四个按钮： 按钮 作用 Play 从头开始运行游戏 States 为这个游戏存档、读档 Launch… 换一段程序来跑，或者在游戏前加载驱动文件 Remove 从应用里卸载这个游戏
documents.s: 第 2 步 —— 安装游戏

documents.t: 这里的游戏是一个形状固定的 .zip： the bundle ───────── PLAY.BAT the entry point - the app runs this <the game files> whatever the game needs __meta.json the name the app shows in the list 就这些。仓库里附送了一个，你可以照着看形状、马上试起来：examples/game-bundle——就是 STARFALL 演示版。把那个文件夹里的 whereq-demo-bundle.zip 拷到手机上装上就行。 至于真正的游戏：还在托管这些废弃 DOS 游戏的站点，一般都直接给 .zip。如果某个游戏的压缩包里只有游戏文件、没有 PLAY.BAT，应用是起不来的——自己写一个 PLAY.BAT 去运行游戏的可执行文件，再把文件夹压一次。

按 Play。 模拟器会重启应用并引导游戏启动，你落到 DOS 提示符： DOSBox 欢迎画面和 C:\> 提示符，下方是屏幕键盘。 输入游戏的名字，按 Enter。从这一刻起就是真正的游戏了——真正的键盘，真正的声音，真正的鼠标。 这是一款 1994 年的 DOS 游戏跑在手机上的样子： Formula 1（Domark，1994）跑在手机上，四周是屏幕键盘。 这是 STARFALL 演示版： STARFALL 的标题画面。 STARFALL 正在游戏中，画面两侧是两块键盘区。 第一次运行游戏时，Android 可能会问要不要允许这个应用发通知。它用通知来提醒你「游戏还在后台」。答哪边都行——拒绝只是少一条提醒： Android 的通知权限对话框。 游戏在跑的时候，按左上角的 File 会把 Files 面板拉到上层，面板上会给正在跑的那个游戏显示一行 Resume： 游戏运行中拉出的 Files 面板，列表上方有 Resume F1。

不用外接实体键盘，因为屏幕键盘就是键盘。横屏时画面两侧会出现两块键盘区，像掌机那样摆：左边是方向键组成的十字键加半边 QWERTY，右边是动作键（Alt、Ctrl、Shift、Space、Enter）和另外半边字母。 两个键可以切换键盘区显示的内容： 键 显示 #+= 标点层 Fn F1–F12、Ins/Del、Home/End、PgUp/PgDn、Caps、PrtSc、Pause 切换之后，那个键会亮着。 #+= 标点层——标点占的就是字母的位置。 Fn 功能层——整排 F 键和编辑键，一个字母键都不用让出来。 修饰键有两种用法。 点一下 Ctrl、Alt 或 Shift，它会保持按下状态等你按下一个键——先 Ctrl 再 C。按住它，它的表现就和一个真正的键一样：手指按着多久它就保持多久，游戏里那些开火键、侧移键正是这么用的，另一只拇指同时操控方向。 鼠标就是屏幕本身。 你的手指就是鼠标：拖动是移动指针，点一下是点击，屏幕上的 RMB 键（左边那块，紧挨 Tab）是鼠标右键——在大多数 DOS 游戏里那代表取消或返回。在画面上按住第二根手指也是同一个意思，而且是在那根手指自己的位置上。 把手机转成竖屏，两块键盘区会折成底部的一条，适合画面高比宽大的游戏。 布局跟着屏幕走。 4:3 的 DOS 画面两侧的黑边，至少要有 116 dp 才放得下一整块手柄区。窄一点的横屏手机仍然放得下——18:9 的黑边有 137 dp——但字母键被挤到大约 24 dp 宽，而 20:9 的屏幕上是 33 dp。十字键和动作键保持原尺寸，挤小的只有字母；#+= 和 Fn 两层同样如此。 同一套布局在 18:9 屏幕上。手柄区照样放得下，但字母键紧了——大约 24 dp 宽， 而 20:9 的屏幕上是 33 dp。 黑边窄到 116 dp 以下，两块手柄区就变成单列。 116 dp 以下，画面旁边已经放不下一整块键盘，于是手柄区变成每边一列键——左边是方向键，右边是动作键——整个 QWERTY 则在需要时从底部折叠起来。 单列布局——每边一列键，DOS 画面仍然占着中间。 左边那列的 ⌨ 键会把 QWERTY 拉出来：从底部升起来，盖住画面的一部分；再按一次同样的键，它就收回去。 同一套布局，QWERTY 从底部折叠起来的样子。键盘图标亮着，再按一次就收起来。 黑边窄到 56 dp 以下，连这也放不下了，键盘就只剩一条贴着屏幕底边的窄条。
documents.s: 第 4 步 —— 键盘和鼠标

documents.t: 有些游戏要的是手柄，不是打字机。Game Mode 把两块键盘区换成一台游戏台式的手柄：八向方向键、一颗轨迹球，外加 DOS 游戏真正用来开火、跳跃和横移的那几个键。 Game Mode。字母键盘没了，换成 D-pad 和轨迹球，还是占着原来那两条黑边。 进出都要一点老派仪式感。 键盘显示着的时候，先打开 Caps Lock——双击 Shift，那个键会亮成蓝色并写着 CAPS——然后在键盘上敲那段 Konami 暗号：↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A，两块键盘区就翻成了 Game Mode。那个 B 和 A 必须是大写：暗号按字母实际打出来的大小写来匹配，小写的 "ba" 只会老老实实地把 "ba" 打进 DOS 提示符。要退出来，就在手柄上再敲一遍同一段暗号：方向键上的 ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← →，然后按 X、Y（这两个面部键替 B 和 A 上场）。手机的返回键同样能把你带回键盘。 左上角那个金色按钮写着当前的档案；点一下轮换，长按打开选择器。每个游戏都记住你上次和它一起用的那一个档案，以及方向键的输出模式。 长按那个金色的档案按钮，选择器就弹出来——三个档案，以及进入映射页面的入口。 档案 左拇指 右拇指 适合 Hybrid（默认） 八向 D-pad 轨迹球 键和鼠标混着来的游戏——Dune II、X-COM、配鼠标的 Doom Action 八向 D-pad FIRE / JUMP / USE / ENT 几个键 键盘街机和射击游戏——Wolf3D、Keen、Prince of Persia Point 大大的 LEFT / RIGHT 鼠标键 轨迹球 纯鼠标游戏——Monkey Island、Civilization、Lemmings Action 档案：FIRE、JUMP、USE 和 ENT，给那些用键盘开火和跳跃的游戏。 Point & click 档案：鼠标键占满左半边，轨迹球占右半边。 轨迹球移动指针的方式像笔记本触控板——划一下动一点，轻点就是点击——而不是一下子跳到你按下去的地方。在 Hybrid 里，按住 L-CLICK（左肩键）同时滚轨迹球，就是框选。
documents.s: Game Mode —— 一台掌机手柄

documents.t: DOS 游戏对「上」这个方向各说各话。D-pad 下面的 ARROWS 按钮轮换手柄到底发什么，应用会按游戏记住你选的那一种： 模式 上 / 下 / 左 / 右 斜向（比如上右） 适合 ARROWS 方向键 ↑ ↓ ← → 同时按两个键（↑ + →） 大多数游戏——凡是读方向键的 NUMPAD 数字小键盘 8 / 2 / 4 / 6 单个键——7 / 9 / 1 / 3 按小键盘做的游戏，斜向自成一个键（很多 roguelike 和小键盘映射的游戏） WASD 字母 W / A / S / D 同时按两个键（W + D） 后来的射击游戏，以及一切绑定了 WASD 的游戏 所以差别有两层：按哪些键，以及斜向怎么发——ARROWS 和 WASD 是把相邻的两个键一起按下去，NUMPAD 则八个方向各有各的键。游戏完全不理方向键的话，八成是模式不对：用 ARROWS 按钮一路换到它有反应为止。

有时候游戏要的键手柄上没有——用 F 开火、用 SPACE 跳跃、拿数字小键盘射击。任何 Game Mode 按键都能改教它发别的键，而且应用会按游戏记住。 长按那个金色的档案按钮（左上角，写着档案名字的那个），选 Remap buttons…。屏幕进入映射模式：顶部一条横幅写着 "Tap a button to remap"，可以改的按键镀着金色描边。点其中一个，会弹出一串按键，挑你想要的。DONE（或者那条横幅）就退出映射模式。 映射模式：金色描边标出了可以改的按键；金色的 FIRE 按钮上得用深褐色描边，否则就看不见了。 可以改 不能改 CTRL、ALT、SHIFT、TAB、STR ◂、STR ▸、SPACE、ENT、USE、JUMP 和 FIRE X 和 Y 两个按钮（它们要回答游戏的 Quit? (Y/N) 提问，也要响应 Konami 暗号）、ESC、D-pad、轨迹球、鼠标键，以及功能键（ARROWS、Fn、1–9、TURBO、SPEED、DRAG、DBL） 改过的按键会显示新键名，而不是原来的名字——FIRE 保留自己的名字，新键显示在它下面。列表里的第一项 Reset to default 可以还原。 重新映射按游戏保存，而且覆盖所有档案：不管你用哪个档案玩，这个游戏都记得每个键该发什么。

存档是把整台机器冻住：CPU、内存、显存、声卡芯片、打开着的 DOS 文件句柄，全都冻住。读档之后，游戏正好停在你离开时的样子——哪怕中间应用被关掉过。 按 File，再按游戏旁边的 States： Save states 面板，三个空档位。 一共有三个档位。按 Save 把当前游戏冻进档位 1，面板会告诉你是什么时候存的： 已存的档位——档位 1，两分钟前。 关掉面板，Files 面板会为这个游戏保留一行 Resume，写明是哪个档位、什么时候存的： Resume starfall-v2 · slot 1 · just now。 Load 把游戏放回去。档位能撑过退出应用，也能撑过手机重启。

存档默认放在应用自己的私有存储里。卸载应用时 Android 会把它删掉——手机丢了、换手机了，也一样。你的游戏和你的存档跟着一起没。 所以应用会问你一次：要不要在你自己掌管的地方再留一份： 首次存档后出现的 Keep your saves safe 提示。 应用自己的对话框里也是同一套说法，随时可以打开看： Saves folder 对话框，尚未设置任何文件夹。 按 Choose folder，系统会问要不要允许这个应用访问手机上的某个文件夹： 系统对文件夹的授权对话框。 选好文件夹，按 USE THIS FOLDER，再按 ALLOW。从这以后每个档位都会压缩一份镜像到那个文件夹里，就放在游戏旁边。 你随时可以在 Config → Saves folder 下查看或更换这个文件夹： 设置对话框。 Saves folder 对话框，已经设置好文件夹。 两点提醒： Android 不允许应用直接占用整个 Download 文件夹，那个权限太宽了。挑别的文件夹就行——Documents 完全可以。 你只需要回答这一次，应用不会再问。
documents.s: 第 6 步 —— 让存档更安全

documents.t: 这就是那个文件夹的用处。 把应用卸载，重新装上，选同一个文件夹。应用会进去一看，你的游戏还在——它们从来就不在应用里面： 应用卸载之后，手机上那个文件夹里的内容。 应用会认出那些没被安装的游戏，问你要不要把它们带回来： Restore games 提示。 按 Restore，它们连名字带存档一起回来： 恢复出来的两个游戏，存档也在。 而存档仍然记得自己是什么时候存的： 恢复出来的档位，仍然写着三分钟前。 最后这一行就是整个功能的意义所在。三分钟前存的存档，就写着三分钟前——哪怕它是从文件夹里重新装回一个新装的版本。

这篇就是指南。仓库里存着同一份文档，以及它背后的一切： 👉 github.com/whereq/whereq-dosbox——源码、示例包、问题追踪，指南本身在 docs/USER-GUIDE.md。 **技术参考**是长文——原生构建怎么做、存档机制怎么把整台机器拍下来、FM 芯片怎么被精确还原、包怎么变成一个跑起来的 DOS 程序、屏幕键盘怎么把按键送进模拟器、以及构建流水线。它是写给工程师看的，不是给拿着手机的人看的。 **发布页**上有 APK 和它的校验和。

没有 DOSBox 项目，这一切都不可能。 DOSBox 由 DOSBox Team 写成——一群志愿者把 1994 年的一套操作系统改造到此后世界造出的每一台机器上都能跑，包括那些当时还不存在的机器。他们让它活过了三十年，并免费交给任何想要的人。WhereQ-DOSBox 只是建在他们工作之上的一层薄薄的壳。原创力、手艺和慷慨完全属于他们。 这个移植基于 Em-DOSBox——Boris Gjenero 做的 DOSBox r4305 的 Emscripten 版，它又来自 Ismail Khatib 最早那次用 Emscripten 编译 DOSBox 的尝试，并且踩着 Alon Zakai 的 Emscripten 工作一路往前。窗口、音频和触摸输入则由 Sam Lantinga 的 SDL2 库承担。 DOSBox 是 DOSBox 项目的商标；这个移植与 DOSBox 团队没有任何隶属或背书关系。 上面每一张截图都是真机，跑的是正式签名的 APK。这里没有任何一张是效果图。

一、平台架构革命：LangGraph驱动的执行引擎​ WhereQ-GPT采用全新的有状态工作流引擎设计，通过LangGraph实现复杂BI查询的智能化编排。平台核心技术栈包括： Python 3.12：利用模式匹配和性能优化 LangGraph 0.1：构建闭环决策工作流 LangChain 0.2：提供AI基础能力组件 Weaviate：多模态向量数据库 OpenAI GPT-4o：最新多模态模型 graph LR A[用户查询] --> B{LangGraph工作流} B --> C[查询理解节点] C --> D[多源向量检索] D --> E[SQL生成节点] E --> F[数据聚合节点] F --> G[可视化决策节点] G --> H{结果满意?} H -- 否 --> C H -- 是 --> I[输出结果]

documents.t: from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END from typing import TypedDict, List, Annotated import operator class QueryState(TypedDict): raw_query: str parsed_query: dict candidate_tables: List[str] sql_query: str query_results: dict visualization_spec: dict workflow = StateGraph(QueryState)

查询解析节点​ from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI def parse_query(state: QueryState): parser_prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(""" 作为BI分析师，请解析查询： {query} 输出JSON结构： {{ "intent": 查询意图, "metrics": [指标列表], "dimensions": [维度列表], "time_range": {{ "start": "YYYY-MM-DD", "end": "YYYY-MM-DD" }} }} """) chain = parser_prompt | ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o") return {"parsed_query": chain.invoke({"query": state["raw_query"]})} 多源向量检索节点​ from langchain_community.vectorstores import Weaviate from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda def retrieve_schemas(state: QueryState): client = weaviate.Client("http://weaviate:8080") vectorstore = Weaviate(client, "BizSchema", "content") # 多模态检索：结合文本和结构化特征 retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever( search_type="hybrid", search_kwargs={ "text_weight": 0.7, "vector_weight": 0.3, "k": 5 } ) # 并行检索不同领域schema domains = ["retail", "finance", "manufacturing"] results = {} for domain in domains: results[domain] = retriever.invoke( f"{state['raw_query']} [DOMAIN:{domain}]" ) return {"candidate_tables": results}

def should_retry(state: QueryState): # 基于结果质量决定是否重试 last_score = state.get("result_score", 0) return last_score < 0.8 # 置信度阈值 def finalize_output(state: QueryState): # 验证结果完整性 required_fields = state["parsed_query"]["metrics"] return all(field in state["query_results"] for field in required_fields) # 构建工作流 workflow.add_node("parse", parse_query) workflow.add_node("retrieve", retrieve_schemas) workflow.add_node("generate_sql", generate_sql) workflow.add_node("execute_query", execute_query) workflow.add_node("visualize", generate_visualization) # 定义边关系 workflow.add_edge("parse", "retrieve") workflow.add_edge("retrieve", "generate_sql") workflow.add_edge("generate_sql", "execute_query") workflow.add_edge("execute_query", "visualize") # 条件循环边 workflow.add_conditional_edges( "visualize", should_retry, {"retry": "retrieve", "end": END} ) # 验证边 workflow.add_edge("visualize", finalize_output) workflow.set_entry_point("parse")

class RetailWorkflow(StateGraph): def __init__(self): super().__init__(QueryState) self.add_node("apply_promo_rules", self._apply_promo_rules) def _apply_promo_rules(self, state: QueryState): # 促销规则引擎集成 promo_chain = ( ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(""" 根据促销规则修正查询： 原始查询：{{query}} 当前结果：{{results}} 可用促销规则： - 买一赠一商品需合并统计 - 跨店满减需计算实际收入 """) | ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4", temperature=0) | StrOutputParser() ) return {"query_results": promo_chain.invoke(state)}

manufacturing_kpis = { "oee": { "formula": "(good_units * ideal_cycle_time) / (production_time * max_speed)", "dependencies": ["production_facts", "machine_specs"] }, "throughput": { "formula": "total_units / active_hours", "vector_path": "manufacturing/kpis/throughput" } } def calculate_kpi(state: QueryState): # 从向量库加载KPI定义 kpi_def = vectorstore.similarity_search( state["parsed_query"]["metrics"][0], filter={"domain": "manufacturing"} ) # 动态公式计算 return {"query_results": eval_kpi(kpi_def, state["query_results"])}

from langgraph.graph import Graph master_graph = Graph() @master_graph.node def route_query(state): # 领域路由 if "sales" in state["raw_query"].lower(): return {"subgraph": "retail"} elif "machine" in state["raw_query"].lower(): return {"subgraph": "manufacturing"} @master_graph.edge("route_query", lambda state: state["subgraph"]) def select_subgraph(state): return state["subgraph"] # 注册子工作流 master_graph.add_subgraph("retail", RetailWorkflow()) master_graph.add_subgraph("manufacturing", ManufacturingWorkflow())

from langgraph.checkpoint import MemorySaver workflow = StateGraph( QueryState, checkpoint=MemorySaver() ) # 从历史状态恢复 def restore_state(query_id): return workflow.get_state(query_id) # 自动保存点 workflow.add_node("savepoint", lambda state: state) workflow.add_edge("generate_sql", "savepoint")

from langgraph.distributed import RayExecutor ray_executor = RayExecutor( workflow.compile(), runtime_env={"pip": ["langchain", "weaviate-client"]} ) future = ray_executor.submit({ "raw_query": "Q3季度各区域销售对比", "session_id": "user123" }) result = future.result()

# Weaviate混合索引配置 class BizSchema(WeaviateClass): class_name = "BizSchema" vectorizer = "multi2vec-clip" properties = [ {"name": "domain", "dataType": ["text"]}, {"name": "formula", "dataType": ["text"]}, { "name": "structural_features", "dataType": ["number[]"], "vectorIndexConfig": { "pq": {"enabled": True} } } ]
from langgraph.cache import SQLiteCache workflow = StateGraph( QueryState, checkpoint=SQLiteCache("whereq_cache.db") )

async def parallel_nodes(state): # 并行执行不依赖的节点 parse_task = asyncio.create_task(parse_query(state)) retrieve_task = asyncio.create_task(retrieve_schemas(state)) parsed, schemas = await asyncio.gather(parse_task, retrieve_task) return {**parsed, **schemas}

用户查询： "对比618和双11大促期间，美妆品类在不同价格带的转化率差异" 工作流执行轨迹： 解析出关键要素： 时间范围：618 vs 双11 品类：美妆 维度：价格带 指标：转化率 LangGraph触发多路径执行： graph TB A[解析查询] --> B[检索促销规则] A --> C[检索产品目录] B --> D[生成促销调整SQL] C --> D D --> E[执行查询] E --> F{数据质量检查} F -- 不满足 --> B F -- 通过 --> G[生成热力图] 最终输出： { "visualization": { "type": "heatmap", "data": { "x": ["0-100元", "100-300元", "300元以上"], "y": ["618", "双11"], "z": [[0.15, 0.22, 0.08], [0.18, 0.25, 0.12]] }, "annotations": [ { "text": "高端产品在双11表现更好", "position": [2, 1] } ] } }

from langgraph.extensions import Plugin class CustomKpiPlugin(Plugin): def __init__(self): super().__init__() self.hooks = { "pre_visualization": self.add_kpi_trendline } def add_kpi_trendline(self, state): # 自动添加趋势线分析 if "trend" in state["parsed_query"]["intent"]: state["visualization_spec"]["config"]["trendline"] = True return state

from langgraph.streaming import StreamingEventHandler class WhereQHandler(StreamingEventHandler): def on_query_parsed(self, data): self.emit("parser", data["parsed_query"]) def on_results_ready(self, data): self.emit("data", data["query_results"]) def on_visualization(self, data): self.emit("viz", data["visualization_spec"]) workflow = StateGraph( QueryState, handlers=[WhereQHandler()] ) WhereQ-GPT通过LangGraph实现的工作流引擎，相比传统BI系统具有以下优势： 动态适应性：根据中间结果自动调整执行路径 领域智能：内置行业特定处理逻辑 可观测性：完整记录决策过程 持续进化：通过检查点机制实现经验积累

🧩 Workflow Overview​ User Input: Receive a natural language question. Embedding: Convert the question into a vector representation. Schema Retrieval: Use FAISS to find relevant database schemas based on the vector. Term Mapping: Map domain-specific terms to database fields using a local knowledge base. Time Parsing: Identify and standardize time expressions in the question. SQL Generation: Use OpenAI's GPT model to generate the SQL query. Execution: Run the SQL query against the database and return results.(Kaggle)
documents.s: WhereQ-GPT with LangGraph and LangChain - II

documents.t: User Input: Receive a natural language question. Embedding: Convert the question into a vector representation. Schema Retrieval: Use FAISS to find relevant database schemas based on the vector. Term Mapping: Map domain-specific terms to database fields using a local knowledge base. Time Parsing: Identify and standardize time expressions in the question. SQL Generation: Use OpenAI's GPT model to generate the SQL query. Execution: Run the SQL query against the database and return results.(Kaggle)
Ensure you have the necessary packages installed:(Introduction | 🦜️🔗 LangChain) pip install langgraph langchain langchain-community openai faiss-cpu

Each step in the workflow is represented as a node in LangGraph. a. Embedding Node​ Converts the user's question into a vector.(YouTube) from langchain.embeddings import OpenAIEmbeddings def embed_question(state): question = state['question'] embedding_model = OpenAIEmbeddings() vector = embedding_model.embed_query(question) state['vector'] = vector return state b. Schema Retrieval Node​ Uses FAISS to find relevant schemas. import faiss import numpy as np def retrieve_schema(state): vector = np.array(state['vector']).astype('float32') D, I = state['faiss_index'].search(np.array([vector]), k=3) matched_schemas = [state['schema_texts'][i] for i in I[0]] state['matched_schemas'] = matched_schemas return state c. Term Mapping Node​ Maps domain-specific terms to database fields. def map_terms(state): question = state['question'] term_mappings = state['term_mappings'] # e.g., {'soft drinks': 'beverages'} for term, field in term_mappings.items(): question = question.replace(term, field) state['mapped_question'] = question return state d. Time Parsing Node​ Identifies and standardizes time expressions. import re from datetime import datetime def parse_time(state): question = state['mapped_question'] # Simple example for Q3 2024 match = re.search(r'Q([1-4]) (\d{4})', question) if match: quarter = int(match.group(1)) year = int(match.group(2)) month_start = (quarter - 1) * 3 + 1 start_date = datetime(year, month_start, 1).strftime('%Y-%m-%d') end_month = month_start + 2 end_date = datetime(year, end_month, 28).strftime('%Y-%m-%d') # Simplified state['time_range'] = (start_date, end_date) else: state['time_range'] = None return state e. SQL Generation Node​ Uses OpenAI's GPT model to generate the SQL query. from langchain.chat_models import ChatOpenAI from langchain.prompts import PromptTemplate def generate_sql(state): llm = ChatOpenAI(model_name="gpt-3.5-turbo") prompt = PromptTemplate.from_template(""" Given the following database schemas: {schemas} And the question: {question} Generate an appropriate SQL query. """) input_prompt = prompt.format( schemas='\n'.join(state['matched_schemas']), question=state['mapped_question'] ) sql_query = llm.predict(input_prompt) state['sql_query'] = sql_query return state f. Execution Node​ Executes the SQL query against the database. import sqlite3 def execute_query(state): conn = sqlite3.connect('your_database.db') cursor = conn.cursor() cursor.execute(state['sql_query']) results = cursor.fetchall() state['results'] = results conn.close() return state

Assemble the nodes into a workflow. from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END graph_builder = StateGraph() graph_builder.add_node("embed_question", embed_question) graph_builder.add_node("retrieve_schema", retrieve_schema) graph_builder.add_node("map_terms", map_terms) graph_builder.add_node("parse_time", parse_time) graph_builder.add_node("generate_sql", generate_sql) graph_builder.add_node("execute_query", execute_query) graph_builder.set_entry_point("embed_question") graph_builder.add_edge("embed_question", "retrieve_schema") graph_builder.add_edge("retrieve_schema", "map_terms") graph_builder.add_edge("map_terms", "parse_time") graph_builder.add_edge("parse_time", "generate_sql") graph_builder.add_edge("generate_sql", "execute_query") graph_builder.add_edge("execute_query", END) graph = graph_builder.compile()

Initialize the state and run the graph. initial_state = { 'question': "Sales statistics for soft drinks in Q3 2024", 'faiss_index': your_faiss_index, 'schema_texts': your_schema_texts, 'term_mappings': {'soft drinks': 'beverages'} } final_state = graph.invoke(initial_state) print(final_state['results'])

Stand on a street in Toronto and look at the address in front of you. A map gives you one claim about it: there is a pin here. A coffee shop. A hospital. A school. Maybe a parking garage. But the place itself is a pile of claims, and the pin is the least interesting one of them. Which school catchment is that address in? Can I walk to a library, and which one? Is the fuel station on the corner charging 1.42or1.42 or 1.42or1.79? Is that building inside a ward, or inside a neighbourhood, or in a ward and a neighbourhood? Did anything happen on this street last week? Every one of those answers is a piece of data, and every one of them lives somewhere else. The school boundaries are in one system, the fuel prices in another, the administrative outlines in a third, the local news in a fourth. The map you are looking at is the result of all of them agreeing.
documents.s: A pin is a very small sentence

documents.t: The thing that surprised me while building it was how much of the work was not the map at all. Drawing pins is the easy half. The hard half is that a map is a join. Every layer needs its own key, its own licence, its own rate limit, its own idea of what a place is — and a POI (a point at an address) is not the same thing as an administrative area (a polygon that contains an address), no matter how casually you can slide one into the other. So the first version of this app had three different ingestion scripts, each one written for its own dataset, each one holding its own API key, each one breaking on its own schedule. That is the shape of the problem, and it is a shape almost every application in the world has: ten apps, ten scrapers, ten nightly failures. The fix was to make the retrieval a layer of its own — one process, one cadence, one place where the outside world is allowed to enter the app. I call it the crawler, and it is the part of this repository I am most pleased with.
documents.s: So I built the part that agrees

documents.t: Everything on the map arrives by being crawled: whereq.cloud — fuel stations and their live prices, the aggregated price series, and the administrative geography: provinces, regions, municipalities, cities, towns, wards and neighbourhoods, with their real outlines. OpenStreetMap — the places around you. Coffee, food, parking, pharmacies, walk-in clinics, plazas, libraries. RSS and JSON feeds — the local news, events, stories and topics that you can switch on in the top-right corner of the map. One account, one key, one rate limit. The whereq.cloud API allows 30 requests a minute, so the two whereq.cloud crawls share a single throttle — two independent limiters would each allow 30/min and would throttle each other into 429s. It rotates through coverage targets round-robin (a country, a province, a city, a map viewport) so a single tick never asks the upstream for a whole continent, and a target that failed is retried on the next tick rather than waiting out its interval. The content crawler is the same idea with a parser attached: it discovers items from the registered sources, normalizes them, extracts the location, geocodes it through a provider chain, classifies them, and upserts them. A feed that goes dark records last_status='error' and the crawl carries on.

Downtown Toronto. On the left: the neighbourhood guide, the local essentials, the quick categories. Below that: the layers — administrative areas, hazards, curated guides, friends, daily routes. Top right: the content the crawler pulled from the feeds. whereq.com is a map-centric location platform. Open it and you see the places around you; open any one of them and you get a proper page — address, hours, categories, photos, the route to it, and the notes people left. Some of what it does today: Places and nearby — a POI map, plus a nearby search that merges everything within a radius into one ranked list. Place cards — a full page per place, written by people, not by a feed. Schools — every school in the coverage area with its catchment boundary, drawn on the map. Hazards — environmental and infrastructure hazards, mapped and reported. Fuel — stations and live prices, crawled from whereq.cloud. Geography — the areas that contain the places, with real outlines. Routes, friends, saved places, notifications — the ordinary social parts of a map app. English, French and Simplified Chinese, throughout.

Frontend — React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind. The typecheck is strict (noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters), and it is the only real gate the frontend has. Backend — FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Pydantic, 18 Alembic migrations. Database — PostgreSQL 17 with PostGIS. Real geometry columns, a GiST index, and point-in-polygon tests that are not fooled by a simplified edge. Licence — MIT, for the whole repository, including the crawler. Tests — 235 of them, and they need no database and no network. The handful that want a live Postgres are opt-in. This post is not the documentation. The documentation is the repository: the setup guide, the crawler guide, the schema, the data sources and their licences. I would rather you read those than take my word for it. 👉 github.com/whereq/WhereQ-com To run it: git clone https://github.com/whereq/WhereQ-com.git cd WhereQ-com cp docker/.env.example docker/.env # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD and SECRET_KEY docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d --build That is the whole stack — PostgreSQL with PostGIS, the migrations, the API, the crawler and the nginx-served frontend. It comes up on localhost:3743. You do not need any keys to build, test or run it. Leave the OIDC provider empty and it runs in anonymous mode with the sign-in control hidden. Leave the whereq.cloud key empty and the fuel panels stay empty and the geography feed falls back to its public tier. The Google Maps key only decides whether the map itself draws.

The repository has one commit. That is not an accident, and it is not a fresh start from a template. I rewrote the history before publishing it, because the history of this app contained things that were never meant to leave my machine — credential literals, an experiment with school data whose licence forbids redistribution, notes to myself about a deployment. A git history is a permanent public record, and deleting a line after the fact does not un-burn it. So the history was rewritten, the private things were purged from every commit, and what is published is the code, the migrations, the CI and the documentation. The old commits do not exist anywhere a reader can reach them. Beyond that, the honest reason is simpler: this map is the piece the rest of the universe reads. It already serves a keyed geocoding API — geocode, autocomplete, reverse geocode, routes, matrix, static maps — so sibling applications can geocode without holding a Google key of their own. If that service is going to be depended on by other people, then the crawler behind it, and the map itself, should be readable by anyone who wants to run their own. If you want to run your own map of your own city, this is a starting point, not a finished product. Take it.
documents.s: Why it is in the world now

documents.t: This app stands on the work of other people, and it would be dishonest to pretend otherwise. whereq.cloud — our own data platform. It provides the fuel stations, the live prices, the price series and the administrative geography this app crawls. The fuel data is licensed and metered; the geography feed is open data. OpenStreetMap contributors — the POI layer, the neighbourhood geometry, and the census subdivisions, under the ODbL 1.0. The attribution travels with every row, and the footer carries it. geoBoundaries — the formal administrative boundaries, under CC-BY 4.0. Google Maps Platform — the map itself, the geocoding fallback and the routing. Their attribution string is required on every map surface and is in the app. geocode.maps.co, LocationIQ, Geocodio and Nominatim — the free geocoding tiers that are tried before the paid provider, so the paid quota is spent only when everything else is exhausted. feedparser and the rest of the Python and JavaScript ecosystems that this repository is built on. The full list is in NOTICE. And to everyone who has reported a wrong pin, a missing pharmacy or a stale price: the map is better because you told me it was wrong. If you run your own copy, or fork it for your own city — I would genuinely like to hear about it.

站在多伦多的一条街上，看着眼前这个门牌号，地图只会告诉你一句话：这里有一枚图钉。一家咖啡馆，一间医院，一所学校，也许还有一个停车场。 但一个地方本身是一大堆话，而图钉是其中最不重要的那句。 这个地址属于哪个学区 catchment？走路能到图书馆吗，是哪一家？街角加油站今天收 1.42 还是 1.79？这栋楼落在 ward 里、neighbourhood 里，还是两者都算？上周这条街上出过什么事？ 这些答案每一条都是一份数据，而每一条都住在别的地方。学校边界在一个系统里，油价在另一个系统里，行政区划在第三个系统里，本地新闻又在第四个系统里。你看到的地图，不过是它们全部对齐之后的结果。
documents.s: 一枚图钉，其实只是一句很小的话
documents.h: #一枚图钉其实只是一句很小的话

documents.t: 做这个应用的时候，最让我意外的是：真正的工作根本不在地图本身。 画图钉是简单的一半。难的一半是，地图本质上是一次 join。每一层都要有自己的键、自己的许可条款、自己的速率限制，还有自己对于「一个地方」的理解——而一个 POI（地址上的一个点）和一个行政区（把地址装进去的一个多边形），根本不是同一种东西，哪怕你可以随手把它们放在同一个下拉菜单里。 所以这个应用的第一版里躺着三个互不相干的抓取脚本，各自为自己的数据集而写，各自握着一把 API key，也各自在某个凌晨三点悄悄坏掉。 几乎世界上每一个应用都长成这个形状：十个应用，十个爬虫，十个每晚都会失败的作业。 解法是把「取数据」本身变成一个独立的层——一个进程、一个节奏、一处允许外部世界进入这个应用的口子。 我把它叫做爬虫，这是整个仓库里我最满意的部分。
documents.s: 所以我把「对齐」这件事单独做成了一个层
documents.h: #所以我把对齐这件事单独做成了一个层

documents.t: 地图上的一切，都是被爬下来的： whereq.cloud —— 加油站及其实时油价、聚合价格序列，以及行政区划：省、区域、市镇、城市、城镇、ward、neighbourhood，还带着它们真实的边界轮廓。 OpenStreetMap —— 你身边的地点。咖啡、餐饮、停车、药房、walk-in clinic、广场、图书馆。 RSS 与 JSON 信息源 —— 也就是地图右上角可以开关的那些本地新闻、活动、故事与话题。 一个账号，一把 key，一份速率配额。whereq.cloud 的 API 每分钟允许 30 次请求，所以两条 whereq.cloud 爬虫共用同一个限流器——两个各自独立的限流器各放行 30 次/分，只会互相把对方顶成 429。它按 coverage target 轮转（一个国家、一个省、一座城市、一个地图视口），所以单次 tick 绝不会向数据源讨要整块大陆；某个 target 失败了，会在下一个 tick 重试，而不是干等一个间隔。 内容爬虫是同一个思路，只是多接了一个解析器：从登记在册的信息源里发现条目，做归一化，抽出地点，用一条 provider 链反查坐标，分类，然后 upsert 进数据库。某条信息源失联时，它只会把该源的 last_status 记为 error，整轮抓取照常继续。

多伦多市中心。左侧：neighbourhood 指南、本地必备、快捷分类；再往下是图层——行政区划、隐患、精选指南、好友、每日路线。右上角：爬虫从信息源拉回来的内容。 whereq.com 是一个以地图为中心的地点平台。打开它，你看到身边的地点；再打开其中任何一个，得到的是一页完整资料——地址、营业时间、分类、照片、到那里的路线，以及人们留下的笔记。 今天它能做的事包括： 地点与附近搜索 —— POI 地图，加上一个把半径内所有东西合并成单一排序列表的附近搜索。 地点卡片 —— 每个地点一页完整页面，由人来写，不是由信息源生成的。 学校 —— 覆盖范围内的每一所学校，连同它的学区边界，直接画在地图上。 隐患 —— 环境与基础设施隐患，标注在地图上，也允许上报。 油价 —— 加油站与实时价格，从 whereq.cloud 爬来。 地理 —— 把地点「装进去」的那些区域，带真实轮廓。 路线、好友、收藏地点、通知 —— 一张地图应用该有的那些社交部分。 英文、法文与简体中文，贯穿整个界面。

前端 —— React 18、TypeScript、Vite、Tailwind。类型检查是严格的（noUnusedLocals、noUnusedParameters），它也是前端唯一真正的关卡。 后端 —— FastAPI、SQLAlchemy、Pydantic，18 个 Alembic migration。 数据库 —— PostgreSQL 17 + PostGIS。真正的 geometry 列、GiST 索引，以及不会被简化边界骗过的点在多边形内判定。 许可 —— MIT，覆盖整个仓库，包括爬虫。 测试 —— 235 个，不需要数据库，也不需要网络；少数几个需要真实 Postgres 的用例是可选开启的。 这篇文章不是文档。 文档是仓库本身：安装指南、爬虫指南、库表结构、数据来源及其许可。我更希望你直接去读那些，而不是听我一面之词。 👉 github.com/whereq/WhereQ-com 跑起来： git clone https://github.com/whereq/WhereQ-com.git cd WhereQ-com cp docker/.env.example docker/.env # 设置 POSTGRES_PASSWORD 和 SECRET_KEY docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d --build 这就是完整的一栈——带 PostGIS 的 PostgreSQL、migration、API、爬虫，以及由 nginx 托管的前端。启动后访问 localhost:3743。 构建、测试、运行都不需要任何 key。 把 OIDC 留空，它就以匿名模式运行，登录入口自动隐藏；把 whereq.cloud 的 key 留空，油价面板就是空的，地理数据则回落到它的公开层。Google Maps 的 key 只决定地图本身画不画得出来。

这个仓库只有 一个 commit。 这不是失误，也不是从模板起的新项目。我在发布前重写了它的历史，因为这个应用的历史里，藏着一些本来就不该离开我电脑的东西——凭据字面量、一场许可证明确不允许再分发的学校数据实验、还有我写给自己看的部署笔记。git 历史是一份永久的公开记录，事情发生之后再删掉一行，并不能把已经泄露的东西收回来。 所以历史被重写，私人的东西从每一个 commit 里清了出去，公开出来的只剩代码、migration、CI 和文档。旧的 commit 不存在于任何读者能触及的地方。 再往下一层，理由其实更朴素：这张地图是整个 WhereQ Universe 里其他应用要读的那一块。它本来就在对外提供一个带密钥的地理编码 API——geocode、autocomplete、反查、路线、matrix、静态地图——好让同门的其他应用不必自己持有 Google key。既然大家都要依赖这个服务，那么它背后的爬虫、以及这张地图本身，就应该让任何想自己跑一份的人读得到。 如果你想为自己所在的城市跑一份自己的地图，这是一份起点，不是一个成品。拿走吧。
documents.s: 为什么现在把它放出来

documents.t: 这个应用站在别人的劳动之上，装作不是那样才是不诚实的。 whereq.cloud —— 我们自己的数据平台。加油站、实时油价、价格序列和行政区划都由它提供，本应用负责爬取。油价数据是授权且计费的；地理数据则是开放数据。 OpenStreetMap 的贡献者们 —— POI 图层、neighbourhood 几何，以及人口普查分区，采用 ODbL 1.0。署名信息随每一行数据一起走，页脚里也有。 geoBoundaries —— 正式的行政边界，采用 CC-BY 4.0。 Google Maps Platform —— 地图本身、作为兜底的地理编码和路线规划。他们的署名格式是每一个地图界面都必须带的，应用里已经带上。 geocode.maps.co、LocationIQ、Geocodio、Nominatim —— 免费的几档地理编码服务，排付费 provider 前面试，这样付费额度只在前面全都用尽时才会被消耗。 feedparser，以及构建这个仓库所依赖的整个 Python 与 JavaScript 生态。完整清单在 NOTICE 里。 也要谢谢那些告诉我图钉画错了、药店漏掉了、油价过期了的人：这张地图之所以更好，是因为你们说它不好。 如果你自己跑起了一份，或者为你的城市改造了它——我很想听听。
A Deep Dive into Kubernetes’ Control Plane Backbone​
Kubernetes chose etcd because it provides strong consistency, fault tolerance, watchability, and simplicity—exactly what a distributed control plane needs.
Before understanding why etcd, we must understand what Kubernetes fundamentally is.
documents.s: 2. What Kubernetes Needs at Its Core

documents.t: A container runtime A scheduler only A deployment tool
A distributed state machine that continuously reconciles desired state with actual state That sentence alone explains why etcd matters.
User declares desired state ↓ Kubernetes stores desired state ↓ Controllers compare desired vs actual ↓ Actions taken to reconcile ↓ State updated
👉 Everything depends on a reliable, consistent source of truth
The data store must hold: Desired state (YAML manifests) Cluster metadata Node status Pod status ConfigMaps Secrets Leases Locks Leader elections This data store is the single source of truth.
documents.s: 4. The Role of the Kubernetes Data Store

documents.t: If the data store is wrong, Kubernetes is wrong. Wrong state → Wrong scheduling Wrong locks → Split brain Wrong config → Cluster outage So Kubernetes needs a store that is: ✔ Always correct ✔ Always consistent ✔ Always available (with quorum) ✔ Observable (watchable) ✔ Deterministic
documents.s: 5. Why This Data Store Is So Critical

documents.t: Let’s eliminate obvious candidates first.
Fast In-memory Eventual consistency No consensus protocol Best-effort durability

Redis write → Master Replica lag possible Failover may lose writes Diagram​ APIServer → Redis ↓ Possible stale read 🚫 Unacceptable for Kubernetes Kubernetes requires linearizable writes, not eventual correctness.
ZooKeeper was a strong candidate.
Strong consistency Leader election Distributed locks Proven correctness

Issue Explanation Operational complexity Hard to operate at scale Watch semantics One-time triggers API ergonomics Not cloud-native Data model Hierarchical, not flexible Tooling Heavy JVM ecosystem ZooKeeper was correct but heavy.
documents.s: Why Kubernetes Did NOT Choose ZooKeeper

documents.t: Distributed Strongly consistent Key-value store Raft consensus Watch-first design
Write acknowledged ↓ Majority of nodes committed ↓ All future reads see it Diagram (Raft)​ Client ↓ Leader ↓ Follower A ↓ Follower B (majority ACK) ✔ No stale reads ✔ No lost writes ✔ No split brain
State S₀ ↓ Event E₁ ↓ State S₁ ↓ Event E₂ ↓ State S₂ etcd guarantees: Ordered events Durable transitions Deterministic replay
documents.s: 11. Kubernetes Control Plane Is a Distributed State Machine

documents.t: This is hugely important.
documents.s: 12. Watch Is a First-Class Primitive in etcd

documents.t: Client sets watch ↓ Key changes ↓ Guaranteed event stream
etcd change ↓ APIServer ↓ Controller ↓ Action Controllers are event-driven, not polling-based.
System Watch Reliability Redis Pub/Sub Best effort ZooKeeper One-shot etcd Continuous, ordered, resumable Only etcd matches Kubernetes needs.
/registry/pods/ns1/podA /registry/services/ns1/svcA /registry/nodes/node1
✔ Easy versioning ✔ Easy compaction ✔ Easy snapshot ✔ Easy migration ZooKeeper’s tree model complicates this.
etcd supports: IF version == X THEN update ELSE fail Kubernetes uses this for: Leader election Resource locking Optimistic concurrency control
Controller A Controller B Controller C Only ONE should be active.
Lease → TTL → automatic expiry Diagram: Controller A holds lease ↓ Crash ↓ Lease expires ↓ Controller B elected
Crash ↓ Restart ↓ State recovered etcd durability is mandatory for cluster recovery.
Writes → WAL ↓ Periodic snapshot
Fast recovery Small snapshots Replayable history Perfect for Kubernetes.
This is HUGE. Nodes die Pods die APIServer restarts As long as etcd survives, Kubernetes reconstructs everything.
documents.s: 19. Kubernetes Can Rebuild the Cluster from etcd Alone

documents.t: Feature Why It Matters gRPC API Performance & tooling TLS everywhere Security Small binary Easy deployment Raft Simple mental model
Low write volume Small objects High read consistency
etcd is not designed for: High QPS counters Large blobs Hot data paths Which aligns perfectly.
3–5 nodes Quorum based Simple backups Predictable behavior Kubernetes admins can reason about failures.
❌ Pod logs ❌ Metrics ❌ Application data ❌ High-frequency events etcd is control plane only.
documents.s: 23. What etcd Is NOT Used For in Kubernetes

documents.t: Criteria ZooKeeper etcd Consistency Strong Strong Watch model Weak Excellent API Heavy Clean Cloud-native No Yes Operational burden High Medium Fit for Kubernetes ❌ ✅
documents.s: 24. Why etcd Won Over ZooKeeper (Final Comparison)

documents.t: etcd = Brain Kubernetes = Nervous System Nodes = Muscles If the brain is wrong, the body fails.

Kubernetes chose etcd because: ✔ Strong consistency ✔ Event-driven watches ✔ Simple, correct semantics ✔ Cloud-native design ✔ Perfect data profile match etcd is not fast—but Kubernetes does not need fast. Kubernetes needs correct.

Short answer up front: ZooKeeper is chosen over etcd when absolute correctness, strict ordering, and coordination semantics matter more than cloud-native ergonomics and operational simplicity. This goes straight to the philosophy and historical trade-offs of distributed systems.
When people say “ZooKeeper is more correct”, they usually mean coordination correctness, not storage correctness.
documents.s: 1. “Correctness” Means Different Things in Different Systems

documents.t: Type Meaning Data correctness Reads return the latest committed value Coordination correctness Ordering, fencing, session semantics are strictly enforced Both etcd and ZooKeeper are data-correct. ZooKeeper is exceptionally strong at coordination correctness.

ZooKeeper was not designed as a KV store. It was designed to solve distributed coordination problems: Leader election Distributed locks Membership tracking Configuration management Barrier synchronization
documents.s: 2. ZooKeeper’s Original Purpose (This Matters a LOT)

documents.t: “If coordination is wrong, the entire distributed system collapses.” This assumption drove extremely conservative design choices.
ZooKeeper has sessions, etcd does not (in the same way).
Client connects ↓ Session established ↓ Ephemeral nodes tied to session ↓ Client dies → session expires → nodes deleted

Lock correctness Leader correctness Membership correctness Diagram​ Client A holds lock ↓ Client A crashes ↓ ZooKeeper deletes ephemeral node ↓ Lock immediately released This is automatic fencing, not optional logic.
ZooKeeper guarantees: Total order of writes Monotonic reads per client No reordering under failure Linearizable operations But more importantly: ZooKeeper exposes ordering as a first-class primitive
documents.s: 4. ZooKeeper’s Ordering Guarantees Are Extremely Strict

documents.t: ZooKeeper can create nodes like: /lock/node-00000001 /lock/node-00000002 /lock/node-00000003 This enables: Fair locks FIFO queues Barrier algorithms etcd cannot do this natively.
You might hear: “etcd has better watches” This is true for data propagation, but false for coordination logic.
documents.s: 6. ZooKeeper Watches vs etcd Watches (Subtle Difference)

documents.t: One-shot Explicit re-registration Tied to session lifecycle Why? Because ZooKeeper forces you to reason about race conditions explicitly. This reduces false assumptions in coordination logic.

ZooKeeper assumes: Network partitions WILL happen Clients WILL crash GC pauses WILL happen So it prefers: Blocking over guessing Failure over inconsistency Simplicity over convenience etcd is conservative too — but ZooKeeper is paranoid.
documents.s: 7. ZooKeeper Is Extremely Conservative by Design

documents.t: Apache Kafka Apache HBase Hadoop YARN Apache Storm Apache Solr Large financial systems Telco control planes These systems care about: ✔ Strict leader fencing ✔ Lock correctness ✔ No split-brain EVER ✔ Predictable failure modes

Dimension ZooKeeper etcd Primary role Coordination service Consistent KV store Session semantics First-class Lease-based Lock safety Extremely strong Strong but simpler Ordering primitives Built-in Limited API philosophy Explicit, low-level Simple, declarative Cloud-native ❌ ✅ Operational simplicity ❌ ✅

Now the flip side. Kubernetes does not need: Sequential znodes Complex lock trees Session-heavy logic Kubernetes needs: ✔ State storage ✔ Event watching ✔ Simple transactions ✔ Declarative reconciliation ZooKeeper would have been overkill and harder to operate.
documents.s: 10. Why Kubernetes Did NOT Choose ZooKeeper

documents.t: ZooKeeper wins when:
documents.s: 11. Why ZooKeeper Is Still the “Primary Option” in Some Domains

documents.t: Examples: Financial trading leader election Distributed job schedulers Metadata services with strict fencing Multi-writer consensus with fairness guarantees In these systems: A single incorrect lock is worse than total outage ZooKeeper optimizes for never being wrong, even if that means being unavailable.
documents.s: You need coordination correctness > everything else

documents.t: If unsure → stop
If quorum exists → continue Both are correct — but ZooKeeper is stricter.
ZooKeeper = Distributed coordination kernel etcd = Distributed state store ZooKeeper acts like a kernel enforcing rules. etcd acts like a database holding truth.

ZooKeeper is chosen over etcd when: Coordination correctness is paramount Leader fencing must be absolute Fair ordering matters Failures must be explicit, not hidden Operational complexity is acceptable etcd is chosen when: State correctness matters Watchability matters Cloud-native ops matter Simplicity matters
If you fear split-brain more than downtime → ZooKeeper If you fear operational complexity more than coordination edge cases → etcd

方面 LangChain LangGraph 学习曲线 平缓（线性思维） 陡峭（图论概念） 调试难度 低（单一执行路径） 高（多路径跟踪） 扩展性 中等（需自定义组件） 高（内置分布式支持） 可视化支持 LangSmith基础跟踪 完整工作流图谱

1. 从LangChain迁移到LangGraph​ # 原LangChain代码 chain = prompt | llm | output_parser # 迁移为LangGraph节点 def chain_node(state): result = chain.invoke(state["input"]) return {"output": result} workflow.add_node("llm_chain", chain_node) 2. 渐进式改造路径​ 保持现有Chain作为原子节点 用LangGraph编排复杂流程 逐步实现状态感知逻辑

LangChain定位： 继续作为LLM集成标准库 发展更丰富的预制工具链 LangGraph方向： 强化分布式执行能力 增加可视化编排界面 企业级状态管理方案 最终决策矩阵： 选择依据 推荐方案 简单问答/检索 LangChain 需要复杂业务流程 LangGraph 已有LangChain大量投资 混合架构 需要持久化会话状态 LangGraph 快速PoC开发 LangChain 两种技术栈本质上是互补关系，现代AI系统通常同时使用： LangChain作为"肌肉"（处理具体任务） LangGraph作为"神经系统"（协调整体行为）

documents.t: User Input: Receive a natural language question. Embedding: Convert the question into a vector representation. Schema Retrieval: Use FAISS to find relevant database schemas based on the vector. Term Mapping: Map domain-specific terms to database fields using a local knowledge base. Time Parsing: Identify and standardize time expressions in the question. SQL Generation: Use OpenAI's GPT model to generate the SQL query. Execution: Run the SQL query against the database and return results.(Kaggle)
Ensure you have the necessary packages installed:(Introduction | 🦜️🔗 LangChain) pip install langgraph langchain langchain-community openai faiss-cpu

Each step in the workflow is represented as a node in LangGraph. a. Embedding Node​ Converts the user's question into a vector.(YouTube) from langchain.embeddings import OpenAIEmbeddings def embed_question(state): question = state['question'] embedding_model = OpenAIEmbeddings() vector = embedding_model.embed_query(question) state['vector'] = vector return state b. Schema Retrieval Node​ Uses FAISS to find relevant schemas. import faiss import numpy as np def retrieve_schema(state): vector = np.array(state['vector']).astype('float32') D, I = state['faiss_index'].search(np.array([vector]), k=3) matched_schemas = [state['schema_texts'][i] for i in I[0]] state['matched_schemas'] = matched_schemas return state c. Term Mapping Node​ Maps domain-specific terms to database fields. def map_terms(state): question = state['question'] term_mappings = state['term_mappings'] # e.g., {'soft drinks': 'beverages'} for term, field in term_mappings.items(): question = question.replace(term, field) state['mapped_question'] = question return state d. Time Parsing Node​ Identifies and standardizes time expressions. import re from datetime import datetime def parse_time(state): question = state['mapped_question'] # Simple example for Q3 2024 match = re.search(r'Q([1-4]) (\d{4})', question) if match: quarter = int(match.group(1)) year = int(match.group(2)) month_start = (quarter - 1) * 3 + 1 start_date = datetime(year, month_start, 1).strftime('%Y-%m-%d') end_month = month_start + 2 end_date = datetime(year, end_month, 28).strftime('%Y-%m-%d') # Simplified state['time_range'] = (start_date, end_date) else: state['time_range'] = None return state e. SQL Generation Node​ Uses OpenAI's GPT model to generate the SQL query. from langchain.chat_models import ChatOpenAI from langchain.prompts import PromptTemplate def generate_sql(state): llm = ChatOpenAI(model_name="gpt-3.5-turbo") prompt = PromptTemplate.from_template(""" Given the following database schemas: {schemas} And the question: {question} Generate an appropriate SQL query. """) input_prompt = prompt.format( schemas='\n'.join(state['matched_schemas']), question=state['mapped_question'] ) sql_query = llm.predict(input_prompt) state['sql_query'] = sql_query return state f. Execution Node​ Executes the SQL query against the database. import sqlite3 def execute_query(state): conn = sqlite3.connect('your_database.db') cursor = conn.cursor() cursor.execute(state['sql_query']) results = cursor.fetchall() state['results'] = results conn.close() return state

Assemble the nodes into a workflow. from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END graph_builder = StateGraph() graph_builder.add_node("embed_question", embed_question) graph_builder.add_node("retrieve_schema", retrieve_schema) graph_builder.add_node("map_terms", map_terms) graph_builder.add_node("parse_time", parse_time) graph_builder.add_node("generate_sql", generate_sql) graph_builder.add_node("execute_query", execute_query) graph_builder.set_entry_point("embed_question") graph_builder.add_edge("embed_question", "retrieve_schema") graph_builder.add_edge("retrieve_schema", "map_terms") graph_builder.add_edge("map_terms", "parse_time") graph_builder.add_edge("parse_time", "generate_sql") graph_builder.add_edge("generate_sql", "execute_query") graph_builder.add_edge("execute_query", END) graph = graph_builder.compile()

Initialize the state and run the graph. initial_state = { 'question': "Sales statistics for soft drinks in Q3 2024", 'faiss_index': your_faiss_index, 'schema_texts': your_schema_texts, 'term_mappings': {'soft drinks': 'beverages'} } final_state = graph.invoke(initial_state) print(final_state['results'])

WhereQ-GPT采用全新的有状态工作流引擎设计，通过LangGraph实现复杂BI查询的智能化编排。平台核心技术栈包括： Python 3.12：利用模式匹配和性能优化 LangGraph 0.1：构建闭环决策工作流 LangChain 0.2：提供AI基础能力组件 Weaviate：多模态向量数据库 OpenAI GPT-4o：最新多模态模型 graph LR A[用户查询] --> B{LangGraph工作流} B --> C[查询理解节点] C --> D[多源向量检索] D --> E[SQL生成节点] E --> F[数据聚合节点] F --> G[可视化决策节点] G --> H{结果满意?} H -- 否 --> C H -- 是 --> I[输出结果]

documents.t: from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END from typing import TypedDict, List, Annotated import operator class QueryState(TypedDict): raw_query: str parsed_query: dict candidate_tables: List[str] sql_query: str query_results: dict visualization_spec: dict workflow = StateGraph(QueryState)

查询解析节点​ from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI def parse_query(state: QueryState): parser_prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(""" 作为BI分析师，请解析查询： {query} 输出JSON结构： {{ "intent": 查询意图, "metrics": [指标列表], "dimensions": [维度列表], "time_range": {{ "start": "YYYY-MM-DD", "end": "YYYY-MM-DD" }} }} """) chain = parser_prompt | ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o") return {"parsed_query": chain.invoke({"query": state["raw_query"]})} 多源向量检索节点​ from langchain_community.vectorstores import Weaviate from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda def retrieve_schemas(state: QueryState): client = weaviate.Client("http://weaviate:8080") vectorstore = Weaviate(client, "BizSchema", "content") # 多模态检索：结合文本和结构化特征 retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever( search_type="hybrid", search_kwargs={ "text_weight": 0.7, "vector_weight": 0.3, "k": 5 } ) # 并行检索不同领域schema domains = ["retail", "finance", "manufacturing"] results = {} for domain in domains: results[domain] = retriever.invoke( f"{state['raw_query']} [DOMAIN:{domain}]" ) return {"candidate_tables": results}

def should_retry(state: QueryState): # 基于结果质量决定是否重试 last_score = state.get("result_score", 0) return last_score < 0.8 # 置信度阈值 def finalize_output(state: QueryState): # 验证结果完整性 required_fields = state["parsed_query"]["metrics"] return all(field in state["query_results"] for field in required_fields) # 构建工作流 workflow.add_node("parse", parse_query) workflow.add_node("retrieve", retrieve_schemas) workflow.add_node("generate_sql", generate_sql) workflow.add_node("execute_query", execute_query) workflow.add_node("visualize", generate_visualization) # 定义边关系 workflow.add_edge("parse", "retrieve") workflow.add_edge("retrieve", "generate_sql") workflow.add_edge("generate_sql", "execute_query") workflow.add_edge("execute_query", "visualize") # 条件循环边 workflow.add_conditional_edges( "visualize", should_retry, {"retry": "retrieve", "end": END} ) # 验证边 workflow.add_edge("visualize", finalize_output) workflow.set_entry_point("parse")

class RetailWorkflow(StateGraph): def __init__(self): super().__init__(QueryState) self.add_node("apply_promo_rules", self._apply_promo_rules) def _apply_promo_rules(self, state: QueryState): # 促销规则引擎集成 promo_chain = ( ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(""" 根据促销规则修正查询： 原始查询：{{query}} 当前结果：{{results}} 可用促销规则： - 买一赠一商品需合并统计 - 跨店满减需计算实际收入 """) | ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4", temperature=0) | StrOutputParser() ) return {"query_results": promo_chain.invoke(state)}

manufacturing_kpis = { "oee": { "formula": "(good_units * ideal_cycle_time) / (production_time * max_speed)", "dependencies": ["production_facts", "machine_specs"] }, "throughput": { "formula": "total_units / active_hours", "vector_path": "manufacturing/kpis/throughput" } } def calculate_kpi(state: QueryState): # 从向量库加载KPI定义 kpi_def = vectorstore.similarity_search( state["parsed_query"]["metrics"][0], filter={"domain": "manufacturing"} ) # 动态公式计算 return {"query_results": eval_kpi(kpi_def, state["query_results"])}

from langgraph.graph import Graph master_graph = Graph() @master_graph.node def route_query(state): # 领域路由 if "sales" in state["raw_query"].lower(): return {"subgraph": "retail"} elif "machine" in state["raw_query"].lower(): return {"subgraph": "manufacturing"} @master_graph.edge("route_query", lambda state: state["subgraph"]) def select_subgraph(state): return state["subgraph"] # 注册子工作流 master_graph.add_subgraph("retail", RetailWorkflow()) master_graph.add_subgraph("manufacturing", ManufacturingWorkflow())

from langgraph.checkpoint import MemorySaver workflow = StateGraph( QueryState, checkpoint=MemorySaver() ) # 从历史状态恢复 def restore_state(query_id): return workflow.get_state(query_id) # 自动保存点 workflow.add_node("savepoint", lambda state: state) workflow.add_edge("generate_sql", "savepoint")

from langgraph.distributed import RayExecutor ray_executor = RayExecutor( workflow.compile(), runtime_env={"pip": ["langchain", "weaviate-client"]} ) future = ray_executor.submit({ "raw_query": "Q3季度各区域销售对比", "session_id": "user123" }) result = future.result()

# Weaviate混合索引配置 class BizSchema(WeaviateClass): class_name = "BizSchema" vectorizer = "multi2vec-clip" properties = [ {"name": "domain", "dataType": ["text"]}, {"name": "formula", "dataType": ["text"]}, { "name": "structural_features", "dataType": ["number[]"], "vectorIndexConfig": { "pq": {"enabled": True} } } ]
from langgraph.cache import SQLiteCache workflow = StateGraph( QueryState, checkpoint=SQLiteCache("whereq_cache.db") )

async def parallel_nodes(state): # 并行执行不依赖的节点 parse_task = asyncio.create_task(parse_query(state)) retrieve_task = asyncio.create_task(retrieve_schemas(state)) parsed, schemas = await asyncio.gather(parse_task, retrieve_task) return {**parsed, **schemas}

用户查询： "对比618和双11大促期间，美妆品类在不同价格带的转化率差异" 工作流执行轨迹： 解析出关键要素： 时间范围：618 vs 双11 品类：美妆 维度：价格带 指标：转化率 LangGraph触发多路径执行： graph TB A[解析查询] --> B[检索促销规则] A --> C[检索产品目录] B --> D[生成促销调整SQL] C --> D D --> E[执行查询] E --> F{数据质量检查} F -- 不满足 --> B F -- 通过 --> G[生成热力图] 最终输出： { "visualization": { "type": "heatmap", "data": { "x": ["0-100元", "100-300元", "300元以上"], "y": ["618", "双11"], "z": [[0.15, 0.22, 0.08], [0.18, 0.25, 0.12]] }, "annotations": [ { "text": "高端产品在双11表现更好", "position": [2, 1] } ] } }

from langgraph.extensions import Plugin class CustomKpiPlugin(Plugin): def __init__(self): super().__init__() self.hooks = { "pre_visualization": self.add_kpi_trendline } def add_kpi_trendline(self, state): # 自动添加趋势线分析 if "trend" in state["parsed_query"]["intent"]: state["visualization_spec"]["config"]["trendline"] = True return state

from langgraph.streaming import StreamingEventHandler class WhereQHandler(StreamingEventHandler): def on_query_parsed(self, data): self.emit("parser", data["parsed_query"]) def on_results_ready(self, data): self.emit("data", data["query_results"]) def on_visualization(self, data): self.emit("viz", data["visualization_spec"]) workflow = StateGraph( QueryState, handlers=[WhereQHandler()] ) WhereQ-GPT通过LangGraph实现的工作流引擎，相比传统BI系统具有以下优势： 动态适应性：根据中间结果自动调整执行路径 领域智能：内置行业特定处理逻辑 可观测性：完整记录决策过程 持续进化：通过检查点机制实现经验积累
